You are an Opus build worker on the Fortress revival, working in a git worktree of /home/user/fortress. Read first, in order — your complete context:

1. /home/user/fortress/CLAUDE.md (env exports; FORTRESS_THREADS=1 for ALL runs; component name == filename)
2. explorations/microgpt-iteration2-plan.md — "Standing design rules", "Verified facts", "Correctness anchors", "Worker discipline" bind you (spec-first; never end at first error; no single-data-point rules; no commits, deliverables to scratchpad AND edits in your worktree)
3. explorations/aliases-units-report.md — the research round you are implementing (esp. Q3, probes p14/p15/p16)
4. explorations/microgpt2-diet-report.md — current state of the flagship
5. explorations/microgpt2.fss — the file you will modify (in YOUR worktree only)

BUILD SHORTCUT (do NOT run ant): the main checkout is already built. Copy its build outputs into your worktree before anything else:
  cp -r /home/user/fortress/ProjectFortress/build $PWD/ProjectFortress/
  cp -r /home/user/fortress/default_repository $PWD/ 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p $PWD/default_repository/caches
then export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD (your worktree) and use $PWD/bin/fortress. Never point FORTRESS_HOME at the main checkout (your edited microgpt2 would pollute its caches).

TASK (approved by Pavol): adopt the two named spaces in explorations/microgpt2.fss, with one mandated design probe first.

**Step 0 — MANDATED PROBE (Pavol's caveat, verbatim: "ProbDist cost (Costs 6 lines plus one duplicated overload) — can't this be eliminated by using other features of Fortress type system like traits?").** Before touching microgpt2.fss, probe whether the duplicated `ProbDist × Mat` juxtaposition body can be eliminated by a shared trait: e.g. a small trait (RowLike or similar) that both Vec and ProbDist extend, declaring an abstract accessor (the underlying List) and defining `opr juxtaposition(r: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec` ONCE at trait or top level — precedent: how MultiplicativeRing hands Value its inherited operators (complex_ring precedent, plan file "Verified facts"). Verify it coexists legally with the `Mat × Vec` direction (the Rank1-excludes-Rank2 mechanism, report Q3.2 case 2 / probe p14_named_spaces.fss — start from a copy of explorations/alias-units-probes/p14_named_spaces.fss). Also check: does the shared trait break the `opr =` definitions, `|x|`, subscripting, or generator integration the carriers rely on? Try at least two designs if the first fails (e.g. operator on the trait as a method vs top-level function on the trait type; `comprises` clause or not). If dedup works: adopt it. If not: record every attempt's error verbatim + spec section consulted, classify (implementation gap / design limit), and fall back to the duplicated overload. Either outcome is page content.

**Step 1 — adopt `KVCache`** per report Q3.2 case 1 / probe p16_kvcache.fss: carrier named KVCache; forward signature becomes (Vec, KVCache, KVCache); absorb emptyHist and the two parallel extension comprehensions into an extend operation. Net lines should be ≤ 0; count them.

**Step 2 — adopt `ProbDist`** per Q3.2 case 2 (with Step 0's outcome): softmax : Vec → ProbDist; nll keeps logits: Vec; sample takes ProbDist. The flagship attention line `attend(q,K,V) = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V` must stay VERBATIM.

**Gates (all mandatory, in your worktree):**
- goldenCheck: run the golden config — 15 logits + mean loss 1.228662661701597 + 5 grads at 1e-9 must PASS (correctness anchor in the plan file).
- A short training run (~30 steps) sanity check, FORTRESS_THREADS=1.
- Recount stripped core lines with the diet report's counting instruments (scratchpad …/diet/strip.py, segments.py if still present; else reimplement the same rules) — report the new core total vs 206 vs Python's 152.

**Step 3 — regenerate affected Fortify figures** in explorations/fortify/ (your worktree): any per-block figure whose signature changed (softmax, attention/forward if KVCache appears in a rendered signature) plus sheet-notation if the carrier roster changed. Recipe in any .tic header (fortick → latex → dvisvgm, light+dark SVGs). Check the renders: KVCache and ProbDist should typeset as words (no underscore-bold needed).

**Step 4 — memo** to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/named-spaces/: report.md — Step 0 outcome with every probe verbatim; diffs summary; line accounting (before/after, what KVCache removed, what ProbDist cost with/without dedup); gate outputs; which figures regenerated; any new traps. Copy your probe .fss files there too. Also copy your final microgpt2.fss and changed fortify files there (belt and braces — the coordinator integrates from your worktree, but the worktree may be cleaned).

Do NOT: touch the presentation HTML (coordinator's job), commit, push, or modify anything in the MAIN checkout. Your worktree edits to explorations/microgpt2.fss and explorations/fortify/* are the deliverable. Be thorough; make report.md self-contained.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. 1	# Fortress revival
2	
3	This is @palimondo's revival of Sun/Oracle's **Fortress** programming language
4	(Guy Steele's HPC language, 2003–2012; interpreter + partial JVM compiler,
5	BSD-licensed). The repo carries the full available git history (5397 commits,
6	root 2007-01-04, HEAD Aug 2012) with pluckyporcupine's Scala 2.10.7/Java 9
7	migration grafted on top as a tree overlay — see the commit messages of the
8	graft commits for lineage and attribution. Working mode: Claude explains the
9	codebase and produces documentation and experiments as we go; Pavol decides
10	what gets committed. The full collaboration protocol — roles, tone, how work
11	is presented, commit discipline, delegation — is in
12	`explorations/protocol.md`; read it at session start.
13	
14	## Build and run (verified: Ubuntu 24.04 container, JDK 25 — current rung)
15	
16	```bash
17	apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant  # JDK 8/11/17/21 also still work (all gated green)
18	export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
19	export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
20	export FORTRESS_HOME=<repo root>
21	unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS                          # proxy trust-store options confuse ant's JVM forks
22	cd $FORTRESS_HOME && ant compileAll              # ~80 s
23	./bin/fortress explorations/claude_demo.fss      # interpreter ("walk") — this works
24	```
25	
26	Toolchain (2026-08-21): Scala 2.13.18 (build.xml drives scalac via
27	`scala.tools.nsc.Main` directly — Scala 2.13 dropped the `scala.tools.ant`
28	tasks), ASM 9.10.1 (vendored in
29	`ProjectFortress/third_party/asm/`; watch out — Fortress's own
30	`asmbytecodeoptimizer.Opcodes` shadows `org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes` in that
31	package), `-source/-target 1.8` and emitted classfiles V1_6 (both now
32	merely conventions — ASM 9 unblocks raising them as a deliberate later
33	step), sources compiled as UTF-8 (all sources were already valid UTF-8;
34	the old ISO-8859-1 javac attributes just mis-decoded comments),
35	work-stealing runtime on stdlib `java.util.concurrent` ForkJoin (vendored
36	jsr166y retired); see `explorations/modernization-plan.md` for the ladder
37	and current rung.
38	
39	Facts that save time:
40	
41	- **Both execution paths work.** `fortress <file>.fss` interprets directly.
42	  The bytecode compiler path (`fortress compile` + `fortress run`) also works
43	  on JDK 8 — pluckyporcupine's "compiled programs don't run" is wrong here —
44	  but has two traps: imported library components (`System`,
45	  `CompilerSystem`) must be explicitly `fortress compile`d into the cache
46	  first, and **stale caches** cause a misleading
47	  `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)` — wipe
48	  `default_repository/caches/*` and recompile in library order (recipe in
49	  `explorations/repo-internals.md`). The compiler is incomplete (some
50	  constructs still `sayWhat`), not broken. See
51	  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
52	- **`ProjectFortress/hello.fss` runs only via the compiler path** — its July
53	  2012 upgrade imports `System.getProperty`/`CompilerSystem.args`, which the
54	  interpreter can't resolve. Use `explorations/*.fss` as interpreter smoke
55	  tests.
56	- **Test suite (2026-08-19): fully green.** `ant testFast` (~1,400 tests
57	  incl. the full compiler suite) and `ant testSystem` (382 interpreter
58	  tests) both pass with zero failures — the first fully green suite in this
59	  lineage (the 2012 mainline ended with 7 red). History and the two fixes:
60	  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
61	- The interpreter requires filename (sans `.fss`) == component name.
62	- If scalac fails with arity errors in `S*Pattern` nodes, the generated AST
63	  sources are stale relative to `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`:
64	  `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast && ant compileAll` regenerates.
65	- Interpreter caches live in `default_repository/caches/` (gitignored); wipe
66	  them if library edits seem to have no effect.
67	- Architecture map, name-resolution rules, cache anatomy, test-harness
68	  mechanics, and git-archaeology techniques: `explorations/repo-internals.md`
69	  — read it before diving into the source.
70	
71	## Layout
72	
73	- Original Fortress tree: everything not listed below — do not modify
74	  casually; it is the historical artifact being revived.
75	- `explorations/` — revival-era experiments and writeups (ours; verified
76	  running programs).
77	- `research/` — the Guy Steele corpus: `research/README.md` is a committed
78	  links-only index; `research/extracts/` holds committed working notes;
79	  `research/decks/` is **gitignored** (copyrighted PDFs, dropped in per
80	  session, never committed).
81	- `Specification/` + `Specification-1.0-frozen/` — the language spec LaTeX
82	  (in-repo, richer than the published PDF; building it is untested).
83	
84	## Project goals (rough order)
85	
86	1. ~~Baseline the 2012 test suite~~ DONE — fully green on JDK 8 (see above).
87	2. Modernization ladder — **approved plan, standing orders, and current rung:
88	   `explorations/modernization-plan.md`** (Scala 2.12 ✓ → JDK 11 → UTF-8 →
89	   jsr166y→j.u.c. → JDK 17/21 → ASM 9 → Scala 2.13 eval; each rung gated on
90	   the fully green suite; CI early).
91	3. Complex numbers: the spec promises ℂ but zero complex arithmetic shipped;
92	   seed is `explorations/complex_ring.fss`.
93	4. Fix the bytecode compiler path — characterized 2026-08-24: the gap is
94	   the compiler's tiny prelude library, not codegen; prioritized worklist
95	   and measured 6.8–8.9× payoff in `explorations/compiled-path-gaps.md`.
96	5. Grow the Steele research corpus (`research/README.md` lists open hunts).
97	6. microgpt.fss — port Karpathy's 243-line dependency-free GPT (scalar
98	   autodiff, char-level transformer) to interpreter Fortress as an
99	   executable-paper showcase; feasibility map and staging:
100	   `explorations/microgpt-port.md`.
101	
102	Claims in old READMEs (root `README.txt`, pluckyporcupine's `README.md`,
103	`NOTES.md`) describe *their* eras, not the current tree — verify against the
104	code before acting on them.

1	# microgpt iteration 2: plan for the from-scratch notation exploration
2	
3	Approved by Pavol 2026-08-26. This file is the complete context for every
4	worker in the run. Read it fully before doing anything.
5	
6	## Mission (approved verbatim in essence)
7	
8	Test Fortress's founding claim on the best possible specimen. The claim:
9	the gap between how ML literature states a transformer's mathematics and
10	how programs implement it is a language defect that Fortress was built
11	to close. The specimen: Karpathy's microgpt, the smallest complete GPT.
12	The test: construct, in running and verified Fortress, the notation that
13	lets each building block of the model be stated so that its typeset form
14	and the literature's own formula sit side by side and the reader can
15	judge the distance **by eye**. The deliverable teaches two things at
16	once and inseparably: how a GPT works (a reader starting from zero
17	leaves understanding it) and how the notation is constructed (what the
18	language gives, what it must be taught, and what it cannot yet say).
19	Where the correspondence fails, the failure is shown and classified —
20	implementation gap (revival worklist) versus design limit. Everything
21	shown runs; correctness is anchored to the Python reference; the
22	process is documented.
23	
24	**Not the mission** (named local minima — do not fall into them):
25	fidelity to Steele's 2015 slide idioms; preservation of any prior
26	rung's code structure (this iteration starts FROM SCRATCH); the golden
27	check as an aesthetic constraint (it is a correctness instrument only);
28	interpreter speed (measured, reported, never steering notation).
29	
30	## Standing design rules (from Pavol, binding)
31	
32	1. **No custom BIG operators** (`BIG OPLUS`, `BIG BOXPLUS`, any new
33	   glyph) unless the form is (a) genuinely the prevalent way ML
34	   literature writes that mathematics, or (b) provably the only working
35	   way in current Fortress, with the spec-vs-implementation gap
36	   documented. The ML literature writes Σ, Π, 𝔼, max — never custom big
37	   operators. Glyph imitation of Σ is not Σ. Default: named functions
38	   (`sum(...)`) over comprehensions; the genuine library `SUM` where
39	   summands are `Number`s (e.g. over `.data` inside a sum-node
40	   constructor).
41	2. **The specification is the first authority** for any language
42	   question: `Specification/` LaTeX sources (byte-identical to
43	   1.0-frozen in all chapters audited so far). Order of authority:
44	   spec → `explorations/expressiveness-review.md` (audited findings
45	   with probes) → library sources → fresh empirical probe. Never end a
46	   design path at the first interpreter error: check what the spec
47	   sanctions (the vector×matrix "impossibility" had a documented
48	   escape, the Meet Rule / `excludes`), then record divergence.
49	3. **No single-data-point rules.** Any claimed constraint ("always
50	   parenthesize X", "Y is impossible") requires either a spec citation
51	   or two independent probes, recorded.
52	
53	## Verified facts (do not re-derive; probes in `explorations/spec-probes/`)
54	
55	- List/comprehension element-type ascriptions `[\T\]` are needed ONLY
56	  when elements' runtime class differs from the target (numeric
57	  literals → `FloatLiteral`; nested `ArrayList[\…\]` under invariant
58	  `List`). For concrete object element types (like an autodiff node)
59	  they are redundant. Return types on definitions are optional
60	  (inference chapter in the spec is a stub; the implementation infers).
61	  The `zip` static argument is mandatory.
62	- The algebraic tower that exists: `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and
63	  `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` only (`FortressLibrary.fss:328,340`).
64	  Extending `MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` with `one`/`TIMES` inherits
65	  juxtaposition, binary minus, `zero` (precedent:
66	  `explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The spec's full
67	  `Monoid…Field` chapter ships only as commented-out
68	  `Library/incomplete/…INCOMPLETE`.
69	- Two juxtaposition (or any operator) overloads on `(List,List)` shapes
70	  are illegal — but **mutually excluding carrier traits make both
71	  directions legal** (library's own Vector/Matrix at
72	  `FortressLibrary.fss:2634,2641` via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; probes
73	  `p7_excludes.fss`, `p14_genwrap.fss` — a six-line carrier object also
74	  buys `|x|`, `x[i]`, `x[r]`, generator integration, `.map`, clean
75	  renders).
76	- `SUM` is closed to user types three ways (library `Number` seal,
77	  spec's no-static-param-overloading rule, desugarer's one-nullary-
78	  registration-per-name). Coercion parses but is unwired. Multifix
79	  dispatch is unimplemented. `Number` already has `SQRT`.
80	- Real parse traps (verified): chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`
81	  (grammatical by design, `concrete-syntax.tex:921`); `^` after a call
82	  or dotted field needs parens; `|w||>` and `/|` need a space; `V`
83	  cannot name a variable while object `V` is in scope. FALSIFIED trap,
84	  do not propagate: "comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need
85	  parens" — they don't.
86	- Interpreter performance law: run everything `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`
87	  (idle-worker micro-forking makes 2 workers slower than 1).
88	- `nat`-parameterized user vectors with dimension-checked ops run
89	  (`p9_natvec.fss`) — available as a design ingredient, not a mandate.
90	
91	## Correctness anchors
92	
93	- The golden check: deterministic-weight config in
94	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` `goldenCheck()` — 15 logits + mean loss
95	  1.228662661701597 + 5 gradients at 1e-9. Any complete candidate must
96	  pass it (values are architecture-level truths, independent of
97	  notation). Nucleus-stage candidates use the lighter analytic checks
98	  (style of `explorations/mgnative_a.fss` run()) or hand-computed
99	  attention values.
100	- Reference implementations for BEHAVIOR only (not style):
101	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` (v1), `microgpt_native.fss`,
102	  `microgpt_paper.fss`. Architecture facts: 1 layer, heads structural,
103	  rmsnorm without gain, no biases, plain relu, causal by history,
104	  Adam β₁ .85 β₂ .99 lr .01 linear decay, BOS=26 vocab 27.
105	
106	## Fitness function
107	
108	For each building block, typeset the Fortress definition with Fortify
109	(recipe in any `explorations/fortify/*.tic` header: fortick → latex →
110	dvisvgm; rasterize with chromium `--headless --no-sandbox --screenshot`)
111	and hold it against the literature's formula for that block:
112	
113	- h⁰ = Wₑ[t] + Wₚ[i]
114	- RMSNorm(x) = x / √(x·x/d + ε)
115	- A(q,kⱼ) = q·kⱼ/√d_k ; weights = softmax over j≤i ; out = Σⱼ pⱼvⱼ
116	  (vector form: softmax(qKᵀ/√d_k)V)
117	- FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁ x)
118	- L = −log softmax(logits)_y
119	- Adam: element-wise update equations (index form IS the literature here)
120	
121	Judged by eye: would a reader of the paper recognize the line? Every
122	departure needs a reason from the classification {implementation gap,
123	design limit, deliberate-with-reason}.
124	
125	## Deliverables ladder (this workflow: nucleus stage)
126	
127	Each design candidate delivers a NUCLEUS, not the full model: the
128	notation layer it proposes plus running, checked implementations of
129	rmsnorm, softmax, one-head attention (score+weights+blend over a
130	history), and ffn, over the candidate's own autodiff value type (a
131	minimal tape engine is fine; reuse of engine A's *concepts* is allowed,
132	code written fresh). Plus: its Fortify render sheet, a rasterized PNG,
133	and a design memo (what the language gave / had to be taught / can't
134	say; every deviation classified; what the full model would look like —
135	sketch the forward pass in the candidate's notation).
136	
137	Full-model implementation, presentation build, and integration happen
138	AFTER Pavol-side judgment of the candidates — not in this workflow.
139	
140	## Presentation (context for memos; built after judgment)
141	
142	The rebuilt page interleaves tightly: short concept prose per block,
143	then immediately the paired lines — the literature's formula and the
144	Fortress definition's render, adjacent, no repetition of the formula in
145	prose, no tan "the paper writes" echo boxes, never a big code block
146	followed by explanation. New content queued: the honest-loss-curve
147	section (explorations/training-dynamics.md + chart) and the
148	PRNG/SplitMix lineage note (Fortress's parallelism → Steele's 2014
149	splittable PRNGs; explorations/prng-findings.md). The three prior rungs
150	(transliteration → index → carriers) remain the notation-ladder
151	exhibit.
152	
153	## Worker discipline
154	
155	Worktree only; `ant compileAll` once (env per CLAUDE.md: JDK 25
156	exports, unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD); no commits, no
157	pushes, no tracked-file modifications; deliverables copied to the
158	session scratchpad under your candidate's name; timings indicative
159	(shared box). Report every dead end with the error verbatim and the
160	spec section consulted.
161	
162	## Judgment (2026-08-26, coordinating session; full brief: candidates-decision-brief.md in session scratchpad, mirrored below in spirit)
163	
164	The model notation is the **carriers ⊕ tower merge**; spartan survives as
165	the page's measurement exhibit (its verified price list of what each line
166	of machinery buys). Decisions on the brief's open questions:
167	
168	1. Axis weighting: fidelity and machinery-as-content together — the merge
169	   with tower's inheritance-ledger narrative serves both mission halves.
170	2. Weights typeset **bold** (`_W1` → 𝐖₁): bold-matrix is a genuine,
171	   prevalent ML register; italic-capital subscripts are unreachable
172	   (spec numeral rule + Fortify roman rule — classified design/toolchain
173	   limit, stated on the page).
174	3. **Adopt `^T`**: the flagship attention line becomes the literature's
175	   own `softmax(q Kᵀ/√d_k) V`; the one-line transpose operator is itself
176	   a teachable exhibit.
177	4. **Keep the visible max-shift**, in tower's form: `StandardMax[\V\]`
178	   opens the genuine library `BIG MAX` (no `.data` leak) — an honest
179	   numerics point Karpathy also keeps, and the counterpoint to sealed Σ.
180	5. **Bind `d = |x|` / use `d_k` fields** so the paper's symbols survive
181	   and `|·|` is never misread as a norm.
182	6. Spartan's price list and falsified-trap hygiene become page content.
183	7. Per-head plumbing stays as comprehensions — the literature's
184	   `head₁…head_h` ellipsis made precise, not hidden behind machinery.
185	8. Render sheets show the machinery (carriers, lifts, extends-clauses
186	   framed as the inheritance ledger; `sum()`'s body framed as the
187	   autodiff-sees-Σ lesson) — the mission's second half is not curated
188	   away.
189	9. Mandated cleanups: define carrier `=` (the reflexive-false landmine);
190	   apply all judge reclassifications (carriers D2/D5, tower's `Vv` and
191	   "library fiat"); engine node named `Value` freeing the letter `V`;
192	   the loose-vs-tight-slash footnote; every full-model claim gated on
193	   the golden check.
194	
195	Build target: `explorations/microgpt2.fss`, plus per-block render
196	figures (one small .tic/.svg per block) for the interleaved page.

1	<!-- Produced by the delegated aliases/units research worker, 2026-08-27.
2	     Probes: explorations/alias-units-probes/ (all run; captured output in

5	
6	# Type aliases, dimensions and units — spec, implementation, and microgpt2
7	
8	Spec read from `Specification/`. Every chapter cited is **byte-identical** in `Specification-1.0-frozen/` (`diff -q` silent on `fortress/preamble.tex`, `basic/types-vals-vars.tex`, `basic/dimensions.tex`, `basic/declarations.tex`, `basic/trait-parameters.tex`, `advanced/defining-dimensions.tex`, `basic-lib/dimensions.tex`).
9	
10	Classification: **(I)** implementation gap · **(D)** design limit (spec itself forbids/omits) · **(S)** spec-declared not-yet-supported.
11	
12	## The one-line answer to both questions
13	
14	The spec's own canonical list of unimplemented features names both, side by side — `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex`:
15	
16	```
17	:56   The not-yet-supported features include:
18	:59   \item multifix operators
19	:63   \item keyword and varargs parameters
20	:79   \item dimensions and units
21	:81   \item type aliases
22	```
23	
24	Note the company: `multifix operators` is expressiveness-review finding 8; `keyword and varargs parameters` is the gap `microgpt2.fss:260-264` already records. **This list is a reliable oracle and is itself page-worthy content**: Fortress shipped a specification of a language larger than its implementation, and said so in print.
25	
26	---
27	
28	# Q1 — Type aliases
29	
30	## Q1.1 The spec has exactly the feature asked for
31	
32	`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:597-623`, section **Type Aliases** (`\seclabel{type-alias}`):
33	
34	```
35	:601  TypeAlias ::= type Id [StaticParams] = Type
36	:605  Fortress allows names to serve as aliases for more complex type
37	:606  instantiations. …
38	:610  Parameterized type aliases are allowed but recursively
39	:611  defined type aliases are not.
40	```
41	
42	Spec's three worked examples (ASCII source `:612-614`, typeset `:616-618`):
43	
44	```
45	type IntList = List[\ZZ64\]
46	type BinOp = Float BY Float -> Float
47	type SimpleFloat[\nat e, nat s\] = DetailedFloat[\Unity,e,s,false,false,false,false,true\]
48	```
49	
50	And decisively for Q3:
51	
52	```
53	:621  All uses of type aliases are expanded before type checking.
54	:622  Type aliases do not define new types nor
55	:623  nominal equivalence relations among types.
56	```
57	
58	`type KVCache = List[\Mat\]` **is** the spec's `type IntList = List[\ZZ64\]` with different names, and it is *transparent* — no new type, no lifting, no unwrapping. That transparency is why it would be cheap, and why nothing else substitutes for it.
59	
60	Legal positions, from the spec's own grammar (`Specification/appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex`):
61	
62	| Position | Spec | Verdict |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| top-level component decl | `:177-184` (`Decl ::= … \| TypeAlias`) | allowed |
65	| API decl | `:189-197`, `basic/components/apis.tex:29` | allowed |
66	| `where` clause constraint | `:513` (`WhereConstraint ::= … \| TypeAlias`) | allowed |
67	| trait/object member | **absent** from the trait-member productions | **not allowed (D)** |
68	
69	Spec's own warnings: `basic/types-vals-vars.tex:18-19` ("Dimensions and units, type aliases … are not yet supported"); `basic/declarations.tex:16-20` (same list, longer). Wanted-but-weaker-than-desired: `appendices/future.tex:75-96` lists **"More powerful type aliases"** (type-level functions, `type Double[\F extends FloatNumber[…]\]…`) as future work — so the 1.0 alias is deliberately the simple expand-before-typecheck kind.
70	
71	## Q1.2 The implementation is half-wired — and the half that exists is the *expansion*
72	
73	| Layer | Status | Evidence |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Fortify (typesetter) | **full** | `Fortify/fortify.el:3998` — `("type" KEYWORD)`. A `type` line would typeset correctly. |
76	| Parser | **full** | `parser/OtherDecl.rats:102-115` builds a real `TypeAlias` node; `parser/Declaration.rats:41-50` admits it in `Decl`/`AbsDecl`. `fortress parse p1_alias_basic.fss` → `Ok`. |
77	| AST | **full** | `nodes/TypeAlias.java`, `WhereTypeAlias.java` + template/ellipses/visitor variants (55 files mention `TypeAlias`) |
78	| **Compiler index** | **DEAD END** | `scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:187` — `case d:TypeAlias => bug("Not yet implemented: " + d)` |
79	| Type analyzer | **implemented, unreachable** | `scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:552-557` *does* expand: `case ti: TypeAliasIndex => walk(substitute(a, params, ti.ast.getTypeDef))`. `compiler/index/TypeAliasIndex.java` exists. Nothing can construct one — IndexBuilder `bug()`s first. |
80	| Interpreter env | **stub** | `interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:987-993` — `forTypeAlias` is `// TODO Auto-generated method stub; return Boolean.valueOf(false);`. Same at `EvalVarsEnvironment.java:109-112`. |
81	| Tests | **parse-only** | Only in-tree use: `ProjectFortress/parser_tests/DeclTest.fss:15` — `type IntList = List[\ZZ32\]`. `parser_tests` is driven by `ParserJUTest.java:34-42`, which only parses. Zero uses in `Library/`. |
82	
83	**So the revival task is small and well-localised:** implement `buildTypeAlias` in `IndexBuilder` (put a `TypeAliasIndex` in `typeConses`) and the already-written `TypeAnalyzer` path takes over statically; the interpreter additionally needs `forTypeAlias` to bind the name (or a pre-walk expansion pass).
84	
85	## Q1.3 Probes (verbatim)
86	
87	**`p1_alias_basic.fss`** — spec's own first example:
88	```
89	type IntList = List[\ZZ64\]
90	sum2(xs: IntList): ZZ64 = SUM [ x <- xs ] x
91	```
92	```
93	** bug! Not yet implemented: TypeAlias at …/p1_alias_basic.fss:10.1
94		at com.sun.fortress.Shell.walk(Shell.java:1166)
95	```
96	`fortress parse` on the same file → `Ok`. **(I)**
97	
98	**`p2_alias_minimal.fss`** (`type Idx = ZZ32`, no imports) — all three paths:
99	- walk → `** bug! Not yet implemented: TypeAlias at …:8.1`
100	- `typecheck` → same + `File p2_alias_minimal.fss has 1 error.`
101	- `compile` → same
102	
103	**`p3_alias_param.fss`** (`type Pair[\T\] = List[\T\]`, spec `:610`) → same bug at `:10.1`. **(I)**
104	
105	**`p7_alias_api.fsi/.fss`** — alias in an API (spec `basic/components/apis.tex:29`) → `** bug! Not yet implemented: TypeAlias at …/p7_alias_api.fsi:6.1`. **(I)** — `IndexBuilder.buildCompilationUnitIndex` is shared by components and apis (`isApi` flag); no api escape hatch.
106	
107	**`p4_alias_where.fss` / `p5_alias_where_used.fss`** — the `where`-clause alias (spec `basic/declarations.tex:237`, grammar `concrete-syntax.tex:513`). p4, alias declared but unused: `f[\T\](x: T): ZZ32 where { type U = T } = 1` → **`f = 1`** (accepted). p5, alias used as a type: `f[\T\](x: U): U where { type U = T } = x` →
108	```
109	…/p5_alias_where_used.fss:10:11:
110	    U is undefined.
111	…/p5_alias_where_used.fss:10:15:
112	    U is undefined.
113	```
114	**(I)** — accepted and silently discarded. Same shape as expressiveness-review finding 2's `p16_covar.fss`.
115	
116	**`p6_alias_in_object.fss`** — alias inside an object body →
117	```
118	null…/p6_alias_in_object.fss:10:7:
119	    Syntax Error
120	```
121	**(D) design limit, not a gap.** The spec's grammar puts `TypeAlias` only in `Decl`/`AbsDecl` (`concrete-syntax.tex:182,194`) and `WhereConstraint` (`:513`) — never in a trait/object member list. `Declaration.rats:41-50` agrees exactly. Nothing was missed.
122	
123	## Q1.4 Nearest working substitutes, probed
124	
125	**A — empty trait extension. Does not work, and cannot.** `p8_trait_subst.fss`:
126	```
127	trait Logits extends List[\RR64\] end
128	peek(x: Logits): RR64 = x[0]
129	… v: List[\RR64\] = <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 2.0|>; peek(v)
130	```
131	```
132	com.sun.fortress.exceptions.ProgramError: …/p8_trait_subst.fss:17:21-26:
133	Unification error: Closure/Constructor for peek param 1 (x:Logits) got arg ArrayList[\RR64\] of type ArrayList[\RR64\]
134	```
135	**(D).** A trait extension makes `Logits <: List[\RR64\]` — the arrow points the wrong way. To make ordinary lists members of `Logits` you would have to edit `Library/List.fss`. This is structurally why the spec has a separate `type` construct, and exactly what `types-vals-vars.tex:622-623` means.
136	
137	**B — carrier object. Works. This is the route.** `p9_carrier_subst.fss`, two six-line carriers, same representation, different names, on the library's generator traits:
138	```
139	object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])      extends { Rank1V, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] } …
140	object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { Rank1V, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] } …
141	softmax(z: Vec): ProbDist = …
142	```
143	```
144	softmax = <|0.09003057317038046, 0.24472847105479767, 0.6652409557748219|>
145	sums to 1.0
146	```
147	Deliberate substitute — but **not an alias**: a new nominal type, values lifted in and unwrapped out at every boundary, no interoperation with the underlying type. (Prior art: expressiveness-review finding 4 / `p14_genwrap.fss`; microgpt2 already uses it for `Vec`/`Mat`.)
148	
149	**C — import alias (`as` / `=>`). Parses, does nothing.** Spec `basic/components/source-code.tex:93` (`AliasedSimpleName ::= Id [as Id]`), `:154-160` for the api form. This is the *only* aliasing mechanism the spec places outside `type`. Three findings:
150	
151	1. **Surface syntax diverges from the spec.** Spec writes `as`; the parser writes `=>` — `Compilation.rats:303-306` grammar comment (`Id (w => w Id)?`) and `Symbol.rats:234` (`transient void match = "=>" / "⇒";`).
152	   ```
153	   import List.{ List as Seq, ... }  →  …/p10_import_as.fss:9:15-36:  Missing comma.
154	   import List.{ List as Seq }       →  …/p11_import_as_only.fss:9:15-24:  Missing comma.
155	   ```
156	   **(I)** — a spec/impl syntax divergence.
157	2. With `=>` the import **parses** but binds nothing in the type namespace (`p12_import_arrow.fss`):
158	   ```
159	   import List.{ List => Seq, ... }
160	   heads(x: Seq[\ZZ32\]): ZZ32 = x[0]
161	   →  …/p12_import_arrow.fss:14:10-11:
162	          Seq is undefined.
163	   ```
164	3. Nor in the value namespace — second data point ruling out "type namespace only" (`p13_import_arrow_value.fss`):
165	   ```
166	   import List.{ emptyList => nil, ... }
167	   →  …:9:26-34:  Function nil is not defined.
168	   ```
169	   **(I).** Even working it would be *partial*: the grammar renames a **name**, never an **instantiation**. There is no way to write `List[\Value\] as Vec`. Only `type` can name an instantiation.
170	
171	**D — a comment.** Always works, costs nothing, checks nothing. `microgpt2.fss:213-217` already does this well. It is the honest baseline against which any carrier's cost must be measured.
172	
173	## Q1.5 Q1 verdict
174	
175	**Fortress specifies type aliases exactly as asked, and the 2012 implementation does not have them.** One unimplemented case (`IndexBuilder.scala:187`), downstream expansion already written and unreachable (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:552-557`). **(I), small, well-localised.** Substitutes: carrier = a different thing (new nominal type); trait extension = **(D)**; alias in a trait body = **(D)**; import alias = another **(I)** and only partial anyway.
176	
177	Proposed revival-worklist rows:
178	
179	| Item | Spec | Evidence | Payoff |
180	|---|---|---|---|
181	| Type aliases (`buildTypeAlias` in IndexBuilder + interpreter binding) | `basic/types-vals-vars.tex:597-623` | `p1/p2/p3/p7`: `** bug! Not yet implemented: TypeAlias`; expansion at `TypeAnalyzer.scala:554` | signatures name spaces (`Logits`, `KVCache`) at zero runtime cost, zero lifting |
182	| Import alias binding (`=>`; and `as` per spec) | `basic/components/source-code.tex:93` | `p12`: `Seq is undefined`; `p13`: `Function nil is not defined`; `p10/p11`: `Missing comma` | renaming imports; fixes a spec/impl syntax divergence |
183	
184	---
185

187

246	:74      if ( a3 instanceof Id ) {

357	# Q3 — Would named types help microgpt2?
358	
359	## Q3.1 Premise, corrected
360	
361	Since `type` aliases do not exist, "adopt type aliases" is not on the table for a *running* deliverable. The live question is: should `microgpt2.fss` grow **more carrier objects** whose only purpose is to name a space? It already answers yes twice — `Vec` (`:136`) and `Mat` (`:148`), with the payoff stated in its own header (`:127-134`).
362	
363	**Units: don't adopt, and they would be noise even if they worked.** ML papers write `x ∈ ℝᵈ`, never `x ∈ ℝᵈ·metre`; the transformer has no physical dimension anywhere. The one place unit-*like* typing would bite — *shape* checking (`d_k` vs `nEmbd` vs `vocab`) — is the `nat`-parameter machinery, not the dimension machinery; it is already recorded as available (expressiveness-review finding 13, `p9_natvec.fss`) and already ruled out for this file, because microgpt2's dimensions are runtime config values (`nEmbd: ZZ32 = 8`, `:366`), not literals. Cite the spec chapters on the page as a spec-vs-implementation exhibit if useful; keep them out of the model.
364	
365	## Q3.2 Where naming would echo the literature's `∈` statements
366	
367	### Case 1 (STRONGEST) — `List[\Mat\]` means two different things
368	
369	`microgpt2.fss` uses the identical spelling for the **per-head weight bundle** `_Wq, _Wk, _Wv: List[\Mat\]` (`:219`) and the **KV cache** `kh, vh: List[\Mat\]` (`:230`), including `forward`'s return `(Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\])` (`:231`). The file needs a five-line comment (`:213-217`) to say which is which. The paper's own noun is *KV cache*, an object with two operations: index by head, extend at right.
370	
371	**Before** (`:230-231`):
372	```
373	forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
374	    : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
375	```
376	**After** (probed, `p16_kvcache.fss`):
377	```
378	step(nHead: ZZ32, x: Vec, kh: KVCache, vh: KVCache): (Vec, KVCache, KVCache) = do
379	```
380	```
381	K after two steps = KVCache<|Mat<|Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>, Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>|>, Mat<|…|>|>
382	|K2[0]| = 2

386	### Case 2 (STRONG) — `softmax : ℝⁿ → Δⁿ⁻¹`
387	
388	Every treatment of the transformer distinguishes logits from a distribution; the attention line's whole point is that softmax's output is a convex weighting. `microgpt2.fss:201` writes `softmax(a: Vec): Vec` — the reader must already know.
389	
390	**Before** (`:201, :208, :300`):
391	```
392	softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do …
393	nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value = do …
394	sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do …
395	```
396	**After** (probed):
397	```
398	softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do …
399	nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value = do …
400	sample(p: ProbDist): ZZ32 = do …
401	```

403	**The structural risk, answered.** `microgpt2.fss:225` is the flagship line:
404	```
405	attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
406	```
407	If softmax returns `ProbDist`, then `softmax(…) V` is a **ProbDist × Mat** juxtaposition needing a new overload that must coexist with the existing `Mat × Vec` and `Vec × Mat` pair (`:165`, `:169`), whose legality rests on `Rank1 excludes Rank2`. Does a *third* `Rank1` carrier break it?

409	**Probed: no.** `p14_named_spaces.fss` declares `Vec` and `ProbDist` (both `Rank1`) and `Mat` (`Rank2`), with all three juxtaposition overloads, and runs the attention line verbatim in shape:
410	```
411	opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = …
412	opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec = …
413	opr juxtaposition(p: ProbDist, m: Mat): Vec = …          (* the new one *)
414	softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = …
415	attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
416	```
417	```
418	softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = ProbDist<|0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431|>
419	attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
420	```

423	**Cost, honestly:** one 6-line carrier **plus one duplicated juxtaposition body** — the `ProbDist × Mat` overload is a verbatim copy of the `Vec × Mat` one, because the two carriers share no supertype carrying that operation. **That duplication is itself the exhibit: it is precisely the price of not having transparent type aliases.** With `type ProbDist = Vec` the overload would not exist at all, the signature would still read `softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist`, and the alias would expand before type checking (`types-vals-vars.tex:621`).

425	### Case 3 (WEAK — do not adopt) — the scalar spaces
426	
427	`ZZ32` in `microgpt2.fss` stands for token ids (`t`, `y`, `bos`), positions (`i`, `pos`), head counts (`nHead`), dimensions (`d_k`, `nEmbd`, `blockSize`), and plain loop indices. Naming these is where a language *with* aliases gives the biggest documentation win for zero cost.
428	
429	Without aliases, probed and running (`p15_scalar_named.fss`):
430	```
431	object TokenId(v: ZZ32) … end
432	object Position(p: ZZ32) … end
433	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\]) …
434	  opr [i: ZZ32]:     Vec = rows[i]
435	  opr [t: TokenId]:  Vec = rows[t.v]        (* COST 1: one subscript overload per space *)
436	  opr [i: Position]: Vec = rows[i.p]
437	end
438	embed(_We: Mat, _Wp: Mat, t: TokenId, i: Position): Vec = …
439	→ h0 = Vec<|3.1, 4.2|>
440	  token ids = <|4, 0, 1|>
441	```
442	The costs are severe and all in the *harness*, where a reader is least helped: `tokenize` (`:294`) returns `List[\TokenId\]`, so `toks[pos+1]` needs `TokenId` arithmetic; `sample` (`:300-304`) computes `|short| MIN (|p| - 1)` in raw `ZZ32` and must wrap; `tid + 97` (`:429`) needs `.v`. Every one is `.v`/`.p` noise on a line that currently reads as arithmetic — and none buys a line that looks more like the paper, because **papers do not write scalar type ascriptions inline**; they write `t ∈ V` once, in prose, which a comment does for free.
443	
444	## Q3.3 Recommendation — **ADOPT NARROWLY: two carriers, not a scheme**
445	
446	1. **`KVCache` — adopt.** Removes the file's one genuine ambiguity, shortens `forward`'s signature to `(Vec, KVCache, KVCache)`, absorbs `emptyHist` and the two parallel extension comprehensions, and costs **net negative lines**. Probed: `p16_kvcache.fss`.
447	2. **`ProbDist` — adopt if the page wants the exhibit.** Makes `softmax : Vec → ProbDist` state the paper's `Δⁿ⁻¹` by eye; `nll` and `sample` then read as consuming a distribution. Costs 6 lines plus one duplicated overload. Probed working against the flagship attention line: `p14_named_spaces.fss`. **Its value here is double**: better signatures *and* a running demonstration of what the missing `type` alias costs — the duplicated overload is the price tag, which serves the mission's machinery-as-content half as directly as the inheritance-ledger narrative.
448	3. **`TokenId` / `Position` / `Logits` / `Embedding` — do not adopt.** `Logits`/`Embedding` would be `Vec` carriers with no operations of their own, paying lifting at every residual-stream arithmetic site (`h0 = _We[t] + _Wp[i]`, `x5 = ffn(x4) + x3`) — pure noise. `TokenId`/`Position` pay `.v`/`.p` across the whole harness for documentation a comment already gives. Probed cost: `p15_scalar_named.fss`.
449	4. **Units — do not adopt.** Not applicable to the mathematics, and unimplemented besides.
450	
451	**What to put on the page instead of adopting more** — one honest paragraph, itself a finding: *Fortress specifies type aliases — `type KVCache = List[\Mat\]`, expanded before type checking, defining no new type — and the 2012 implementation stops one line short of them (`IndexBuilder.scala:187`), with the expansion machinery already written and unreachable. So a Fortress signature can name a space only by minting a new type, and the cost of minting shows up as a duplicated `ProbDist × Mat` overload next to the `Vec × Mat` one. The literature's `p ∈ Δⁿ⁻¹` costs six lines and a copied operator here; with the alias it would have cost nothing.* That is a paired before/after a reader can judge by eye — exactly the fitness function.

60	(* Value is a multiplicative ring and a StandardMax; saying so buys
61	   juxtaposition (= TIMES), binary minus (= self + (-o)), zero, and the
62	   library's genuine BIG MAX, all as trait defaults (precedents:
63	   explorations/complex_ring.fss for the ring; the tower nucleus for MAX). *)
64	object Value(var data: RR64, children: List[\Value\], grads: List[\RR64\])
65	       extends { MultiplicativeRing[\Value\], StandardMax[\Value\] }
66	  getter one(): Value = konst(1.0)
67	  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
68	  var visited: Boolean := false
69	  opr +(self, o: Value): Value = Value(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
70	  opr +(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data + c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
71	  opr TIMES(self, o: Value): Value =
72	    Value(data o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
73	  opr -(self): Value = Value(-data, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
74	  opr /(self, o: Value): Value =
75	    Value(data / o.data, <| self, o |>,
76	          <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
77	  opr /(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data / c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c|>)
78	  opr /(self, n: ZZ32): Value = self / (n 1.0)
79	  opr ^ (self, n: RR64): Value = Value(data^n, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
80	  opr MAX(self, o: Value): Value = if data >= o.data then self else o end
81	end

83	konst(d: RR64): Value = Value(d, emptyList[\Value\](), emptyList[\RR64\]())
84	
85	exp(v: Value): Value = Value(exp v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] exp v.data|>)
86	log(v: Value): Value = Value(log v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0/v.data|>)
87	relu(v: Value): Value = if v.data > 0.0
88	                        then Value(v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
89	                        else Value(0.0, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 0.0|>) end
90	opr SQRT(u: Value): Value = u^0.5

92	(* Sigma as the literature writes it: a named function, one n-ary Sum
93	   node; the forward value is the genuine library SUM over the addends'
94	   data (they are Numbers), folded sequentially (FP addition is not
95	   associative; the fold order is the reproducibility contract);
96	   d(sum)/d(addend_j) = 1. *)
97	sum(addends: List[\Value\]): Value =
98	  Value(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)
99	sum(x: Vec): Value = sum(x.xs)

101	object Topo()
102	  var items: List[\Value\] := emptyList[\Value\]()
103	  build(v: Value): () = do
104	    if NOT v.visited then
105	      v.visited := true
106	      for ch <- seq(v.children) do self.build(ch) end
107	      items := items.addRight(v)
108	    end
109	  end
110	end
111	
112	(* backpropagation over the reverse topological order; the visited marks
113	   are the engine's own scratch, so the engine clears them -- nothing
114	   outside this function ever needs to know they exist *)
115	backward(root: Value): () = do
116	  t = Topo()
117	  t.build(root)
118	  root.grad := 1.0
119	  for v <- seq(t.items.reverse) do
120	    for (ch, lg) <- seq(v.children.zip[\RR64\](v.grads)) do
121	      ch.grad := ch.grad + lg v.grad
122	    end
123	  end
124	  for v <- t.items do v.visited := false end
125	end

127	(* ---------- the carriers: library citizens ----------
128	   Vec/Mat wrap List; extending the library's own Rank1/Rank2 makes them
129	   mutually excluding, so BOTH juxtaposition directions are legal
130	   overloads; ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed buy |x|, x[i], zip, and full
131	   generator integration (u <- x, BIG ops over x) from three one-line
132	   members; AdditiveGroup gives Vec inherited binary minus and zero from
133	   + and unary -.  Carrier = is defined because HasRank's default
134	   equality is constant false -- even x = x. *)

136	object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])
137	    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\],
138	              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
139	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
140	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
141	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = xs[i]
142	  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\Value\](y) |>)
143	  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
144	  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
145	    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] ((xs[m]).data = y[m].data))
146	end
147	
148	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
149	    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
150	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
151	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
152	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
153	  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
154	  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
155	    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
156	end

162	opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): Value = sum(<| u[m] w[m] | m <- u.indices |>)
163	
164	(* (W x)_r = W_r DOT x *)
165	opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| r DOT x | r <- w |>)
166	
167	(* (p M)_c = SUM_j p_j M_j_c -- the OTHER direction, legal because
168	   Rank1 excludes Rank2 *)
169	opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
170	  Vec(<| sum(<| p[j] (m[j])[c] | j <- p.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

173	   "typically used to signify matrix transposition" (basic/operators/intro.tex) *)
174	opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
175	  Mat(<| Vec(<| (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

178	opr -(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u - s | u <- x |>)
179	opr /(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u / s | u <- x |>)
180	opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| u / c | u <- x |>)
181	relu(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| relu u | u <- x |>)
182	exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| exp u | u <- x |>)

187	epsilon: RR64 = 0.00001

189	(* RMSNorm(x) = x / SQRT(x.x/d + eps) -- no learnable gain; d is the
190	   dimension of x (|x| is length here, not a norm) *)
191	rmsnorm(x: Vec): Vec = do
192	  d = |x|
193	  x / SQRT((x DOT x) / d + epsilon)

196	(* softmax(a)_j = e^(a_j - m) / SUM_k e^(a_k - m): the stabilizing shift
197	   m = max a is the library's own BIG MAX (Value extends StandardMax), the
198	   pointwise e^(a - m) uses Value's inherited minus, and
199	   softmax(a) = softmax(a - m) is an identity, so the shift changes no
200	   number the mathematics defines. *)
201	softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do
202	  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
203	  e = exp(a - m)
204	  e / sum(e)
205	end

361	run() = do

363	
364	  (* config: BOS = 26, vocab a-z + BOS (names.txt is strictly a-z) *)
365	  vocab: ZZ32 = 27; bos: ZZ32 = 26; maxDocs: ZZ32 = 2000
366	  nEmbd: ZZ32 = 8; nHead: ZZ32 = 2; hs: ZZ32 = nEmbd DIV nHead
367	  blockSize: ZZ32 = 8; numSteps: ZZ32 = 30; temp: RR64 = 0.5
368	
369	  docs = readDocs("explorations/names.txt", maxDocs)
370	  println("num docs: " |docs| "  vocab: " vocab)
371	
372	  g = Model(nHead, hs, gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd), gaussMat(blockSize, nEmbd),
373	            gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd), gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd),
374	            gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd), gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd),
375	            gaussMat(nEmbd, nEmbd), gaussMat(4 nEmbd, nEmbd),
376	            gaussMat(nEmbd, 4 nEmbd))
377	  params = g.params(); nP: ZZ32 = |params|
378	  println("num params: " nP)
379	
380	  (* Adam: m_t = b1 m_{t-1} + (1-b1) g_t;  v_t = b2 v_{t-1} + (1-b2) g_t^2;
381	     mHat = m_t/(1-b1^t);  vHat = v_t/(1-b2^t);  w -= lr_t mHat/(SQRT vHat + eps).
382	     Index-form RR64 on purpose: the literature's Adam IS elementwise
383	     index arithmetic -- and elementwise means independent, so the sweep
384	     over i is an unordered for; only the step loop below is seq. *)
385	  lr0 = 0.01; beta1 = 0.85; beta2 = 0.99; epsA = 0.00000001
386	  mBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)
387	  vBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)
388	
389	  t0 = nanoTime()
390	  for step <- seq(0#numSteps) do
391	    toks = tokenize(docs[step REM |docs|], bos)
392	    n = blockSize MIN (|toks| - 1)
393	    var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(nHead), emptyHist(nHead))
394	    var losses: List[\Value\] := emptyList[\Value\]()
395	    for pos <- seq(0#n) do
396	      (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(toks[pos], pos, kh, vh)
397	      kh := kh2; vh := vh2
398	      losses := losses.addRight(nll(logits, toks[pos + 1]))
399	    end
400	    loss = sum(losses) / (n 1.0)
401	    backward(loss)
402	    lrT = lr0 (1.0 - (step 1.0) / (numSteps 1.0))
403	    st = (step 1.0) + 1.0
404	    for i <- 0#nP do
405	      p = params[i]
406	      mBuf[i] := beta1 mBuf[i] + (1.0 - beta1) (p.grad)
407	      vBuf[i] := beta2 vBuf[i] + (1.0 - beta2) (p.grad)^2.0
408	      mHat = mBuf[i] / (1.0 - beta1^st)
409	      vHat = vBuf[i] / (1.0 - beta2^st)
410	      p.data := p.data - (lrT mHat) / ((vHat^0.5) + epsA)
411	      p.grad := 0.0
412	    end
413	    el = (((nanoTime() - t0) + 500000) DIV 1000000)
414	    println("step " (step + 1) " / " numSteps "  loss " loss.data "  elapsed " el " ms")
415	  end
416	  println("s/step: " (((nanoTime() - t0) 1.0) / (numSteps 1000000000.0)))
417	
418	  (* inference: temperature sampling.  A sample stops at the first BOS,
419	     and tid = bos is exactly that condition once past position 0. *)
420	  println("--- inference ---")
421	  for s <- seq(1#10) do
422	    var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(nHead), emptyHist(nHead))
423	    var (tid, out): (ZZ32, String) := (bos, "")
424	    for pos <- seq(0#blockSize) do
425	      if pos = 0 OR tid =/= bos then
426	        (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(tid, pos, kh, vh)
427	        kh := kh2; vh := vh2
428	        tid := sample(softmax(logits / temp))
429	        if tid =/= bos then out := out || char(tid + 97) end
430	      end
431	    end
432	    println("sample " s ": " out)
433	  end
434	end

80	## Changes, one by one
81	
82	### 1. Adam per-parameter loop de-`seq`ed (mandated)
83	
84	`for i <- seq(0#nP)` → `for i <- 0#nP`. The updates are independent
85	(distinct array slots, distinct `Value` objects, no cross-element reads), so
86	the sweep is genuinely unordered and now says so. The step loop stays `seq`
87	— it is a real recurrence. Comment in the file states the distinction.
88	
89	To make that honest, the loop had to stop touching engine state: the old
90	body ended with `p.visited := false`, an engine scratch flag leaking into
91	the optimizer. `backward` now clears its own marks
92	(`for v <- t.items do v.visited := false end`, +1 engine line) and the
93	optimizer body is exactly Python's six statements. Cost measured below.
94	
95	Also collapsed in the same loop: `g1`/`g2` temporaries removed (`(p.grad)`
96	inline — the parens are load-bearing, `^` after a dotted field needs them),
97	and the repeated `(step 1.0) + 1.0` hoisted to `st`. 12 body lines → 8.
98	
99	### 2. Data loading and tokenizer condensed
100	
101	- `readDocs(path, k)` — a named 5-line function replacing 7 inline lines in
102	  `run()`; drops the `if |l| > 0` guard (verified: names.txt has no empty
103	  lines — a `lines()` comprehension over the file yields 32033 strings with
104	  and without the guard).
105	- `tokenize(doc, bos)` — 2 lines, one comprehension:
106	  `<|[\ZZ32\] bos|> || <| c.codePoint() - 97 | c <- doc |> || <|[\ZZ32\] bos|>`,
107	  the direct analogue of Karpathy's
108	  `[BOS] + [uchars.index(ch) for ch in doc] + [BOS]`. `String` extends
109	  `ZeroIndexed[\Char\]`/`DelegatedIndexed`, so `c <- doc` just works. This
110	  replaces a 2-line `array(...).fill(fn (i) => if i = 0 OR i = len+1 …)`
111	  and lets `n = blockSize MIN (|toks| - 1)` be Python's own line.
112	
113	**The `lines()` comprehension was tried and rejected — with a measurement.**
114	`docs = <| l | l <- seq(FileReadStream(path).lines()), |l| > 0 |>[0#maxDocs]`
115	parses and is correct, but on names.txt (32033 lines) it dies under the
116	launcher's default `-Xss32m`:
117	
118	    Exception in thread "main" java.lang.BootstrapMethodError
119	    …
120	    Caused by: java.lang.StackOverflowError
121	      at java.base/java.lang.invoke.InvokerBytecodeGenerator.emitPushArguments
122	
123	It runs with `-Xss64m`. The overflow is the **comprehension size, not the
124	file**: `<| i | i <- seq(0#32033) |>` overflows identically
125	(`probes/pd5.fss`), while a plain `for l <- seq(fr.lines())` over the same
126	32033 lines is fine (`probes/pd3.fss`). `File.fsi`'s `lines(n)` is a
127	read-ahead chunk size, not a count (`Library/File.fsi:56–80`), and the
128	library has no `take`/`limit` generator combinator, so a bounded read is a
129	loop. A `label`/`exit` version works (`probes/pd6.fss`, sanctioned by
130	`File.fsi`'s own note that the sequential file generators may be escaped by
131	`label`/`exit`) but costs 9 lines to the `while`-loop's 5. The `while` form
132	shipped; the finding is recorded in the file's comment.
133	
134	Second-order finding worth carrying: on JDK 25 the interpreter's error
135	*formatter* itself blows up on a deep error (`ErrorMsgMaker` →
136	`StringConcatException: Generator failed` → `StackOverflowError`), so the
137	real message is buried 3000 stack lines down under a `BootstrapMethodError`.
138	`JAVA_FLAGS="… -Djava.lang.invoke.stringConcat=BC_SB"` did **not** fix it;
139	raising `-Xss` did. Any worker chasing a `BootstrapMethodError` from
140	`bin/fortress` should suspect stack depth first.

142	### 3. Sampling extracted and restated
143	
144	The 12-line inline cumulative scan (`cum`/`pick`/`done` flag, `if NOT done`
145	guard) became a 5-line named function stated as its own formula:
146	
147	    sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do
148	      r = random(1.0)
149	      short = <| j | j <- p.indices, (SUM[i <- seq(0#(j + 1))] (p[i]).data) < r |>
150	      |short| MIN (|p| - 1)
151	    end
152	
153	— the inverse-CDF rule as a *count*: the index is the number of prefix sums
154	that fall short of the draw. `MIN (|p| - 1)` is exactly v1's floating-point
155	fallback (`var pick := vocab - 1`). O(n²) in the vocabulary (27), invisible.
156	
157	The inference loop lost its `stop` flag too: `if pos = 0 OR tid =/= bos`
158	*is* the stop condition once past position 0, since `tid` only becomes BOS
159	by being sampled. 28 lines → 15.

183	### 5. Keyword-parameter defaults: a new implementation gap
184	
185	The prettier form of the weight init is Karpathy's own —
186	`matrix = lambda nout, nin, std=0.08`. The spec sanctions it:
187	`Specification/basic/functions.tex:155–172` ("a keyword parameter must be
188	declared with a *default* expression … specified after an `=` sign"). It
189	parses in Fortress and then dies in the interpreter (`probes/pd7.fss`):
190	
191	    scale(x: RR64, std: RR64 = 0.08): RR64 = x std

194	    ** bug! The number of parameters (2) does not match with the number of
195	    arguments (1).

198	front-end accepts it, evaluator does not. The workaround shipped is the

270	   `Value`'s `data`, `grad`, `visited` are declared without `var` in the
271	   api; the component keeps them mutable. The interpreter accepts the
272	   asymmetry, and `goldenCheck` only *reads* them. (An importer that needed

1	(* Q3 probe: since `type` aliases do not exist (p1/p2/p3/p7), the only working
2	   way to name a space in microgpt2's design is ANOTHER CARRIER OBJECT.  This
3	   probe asks the decisive structural question: does adding a third Rank1
4	   carrier (ProbDist) break the flagship's excludes-based overload structure?
5	
6	   microgpt2.fss declares (lines 165, 169):
7	       opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec
8	       opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec
9	   legal because Rank1 excludes Rank2 (FortressLibrary.fss:1599).
10	   If softmax returns ProbDist rather than Vec, then microgpt2.fss:225
11	       attend(q,K,V) = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
12	   becomes a ProbDist x Mat juxtaposition and needs its own overload, which
13	   must coexist with the Vec x Mat one.  Two distinct object types under the
14	   same rank trait: is that a legal overloading?
15	
16	   Element type is RR64 here (no autodiff tape) -- overload resolution among
17	   carriers does not depend on the element type; the shapes are microgpt2's. *)
18	component p14_named_spaces
19	import List.{...}
20	export Executable
21	
22	object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])
23	    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\],
24	              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
25	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
26	  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
27	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
28	  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
29	  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\RR64\](y) |>)
30	  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] -u | u <- xs |>)
31	end
32	
33	(* a named space with the SAME representation and a DIFFERENT name:
34	   the paper's  p in Delta^{n-1}  rather than  p in RR^n  *)
35	object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\])
36	    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
37	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
38	  getter asString(): String = "ProbDist" xs
39	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
40	  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
41	end
42	
43	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
44	    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
45	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
46	  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
47	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
48	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
49	end
50	
51	opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): RR64 = SUM[m <- u.indices] (u[m] w[m])
52	opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] r DOT x | r <- w |>)
53	opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
54	  Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
55	
56	(* THE NEW OVERLOAD the named space forces: ProbDist x Mat *)
57	opr juxtaposition(p: ProbDist, m: Mat): Vec =
58	  Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
59	
60	opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
61	  Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
62	
63	opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u / c | u <- x |>)
64	opr -(x: Vec, s: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u - s | u <- x |>)
65	exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] exp u | u <- x |>)
66	
67	(* the signature now states the paper's own membership:
68	     softmax : RR^n -> Delta^{n-1}                                        *)
69	softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
70	  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
71	  e = exp(a - m)
72	  s = SUM[u <- e] u
73	  ProbDist(<|[\RR64\] u / s | u <- e |>)
74	end
75	
76	(* microgpt2.fss:225 verbatim in shape, now typed with named spaces *)
77	attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
78	
79	run() = do
80	  q  = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>)
81	  K  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.0, 1.0|>) |>)
82	  V  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 3.0, 4.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 5.0, 6.0|>) |>)
83	  println("softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = " softmax(q K^T / SQRT 2))
84	  println("attend = " attend(q, K, V, 2))
85	end

1	(* Q3 probe: the one place in microgpt2.fss where the SAME spelled type means
2	   two different things.  List[\Mat\] is BOTH
3	     - the per-head weight bundle   _Wq, _Wk, _Wv : List[\Mat\]   (line 219)
4	     - the per-head KV history      kh, vh        : List[\Mat\]   (line 230)
5	   and forward's return type is the opaque (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]).
6	   With no `type` alias, a carrier object is again the route -- and here it is
7	   cheap, because a KV cache is only ever indexed by head and extended at the
8	   right, exactly the two operations a carrier declares in two lines. *)
9	component p16_kvcache
10	import List.{...}
11	export Executable
12	
13	object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])
14	    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
15	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
16	  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
17	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
18	  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
19	end
20	
21	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
22	    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
23	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
24	  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
25	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
26	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
27	  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
28	end
29	
30	(* the named space: one cache, one Mat of history per head *)
31	object KVCache(heads: List[\Mat\])
32	    extends { ZeroIndexed[\Mat\], DelegatedIndexed[\Mat,ZZ32\] }
33	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |heads|
34	  getter asString(): String = "KVCache" heads
35	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|
36	  opr [h: ZZ32]: Mat = heads[h]
37	  extend(ks: List[\Vec\]): KVCache =
38	    KVCache(<| (heads[h]).addRight(ks[h]) | h <- self.indices |>)
39	end
40	
41	emptyCache(nh: ZZ32): KVCache = KVCache(<| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>)
42	
43	(* before:  forward(...) : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\])
44	   after :  forward(...) : (Vec, KVCache, KVCache)                        *)
45	step(nHead: ZZ32, x: Vec, kh: KVCache, vh: KVCache): (Vec, KVCache, KVCache) = do
46	  K = kh.extend(<| x | h <- 0#nHead |>)
47	  V = vh.extend(<| x | h <- 0#nHead |>)
48	  (x, K, V)
49	end
50	
51	run() = do
52	  x = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 2.0|>)
53	  (y, K, V) = step(2, x, emptyCache(2), emptyCache(2))
54	  (y2, K2, V2) = step(2, x, K, V)
55	  println("K after two steps = " K2)
56	  println("|K2[0]| = " |K2[0]|)
57	end
58	
59	end

trait HasRank extends Equality[\HasRank\] excludes { Number, AnyMaybe }
  (** \vspace{-4ex} NOT YET: %comprises Array[\T,E,I\]
                              where [\T,E,I\]{ T extends Array[\T,E,I\] }% *)

end

(* Declared Rank-n-ness *)
trait Rank[\ nat n \] extends HasRank
  rank():ZZ32 = n
end

(* Potemkin exclusion traits.  Really we just want to say that
 * Rank[\n\] excludes Rank[\m\] where { m =/= n }, but we can't yet. *)

trait Rank1 extends { Rank[\1\]} excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }
end

trait Rank2 extends { Rank[\2\]} excludes { Rank3, Number, String }
end

trait Rank3 extends { Rank[\3\]} excludes { Number, String }
end

(* The trait Indexed_i[\n\] indicates that something has an i^th
 * dimension of size n.  In general anything which extends Indexed_i
 * must also extend Indexed_j for j < i. *)
                exit found with Just[\I\](i)
            end
            Nothing[\I\]
        end found
end

trait ZeroIndexed[\E\] extends Indexed[\E,ZZ32\]
    getter bounds(): CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self|
    zip[\F\](g:ZeroIndexed[\F\]):ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\] =
        DefaultZip[\E,F\](self,g)
    opr[r:Range[\ZZ32\]] : ZeroIndexed[\E\]
    opr[_:TrivialOpenRange] : ZeroIndexed[\E\] = self
end

object DefaultZip[\E,F\](e:ZeroIndexed[\E\],f:ZeroIndexed[\F\])
        extends { ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\], DelegatedIndexed[\(E,F),ZZ32\] }
    getter size(): ZZ32 = |self|
    getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] =
        if |e| <= |f| then e.indices else f.indices end
    opr |self| : ZZ32 = |e| MIN |f|
    opr[i:ZZ32]:(E,F) = (e[i],f[i])
    opr[r:Range[\ZZ32\]] : ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\] =
        DefaultZip[\E,F\](e[r],f[r])
end

trait LexicographicOrder[\T extends LexicographicOrder[\T,E\],E\]
        extends { StandardTotalOrder[\T\], ZeroIndexed[\E\] }
    opr CMP(self, other:T): TotalComparison =
        self.zip[\E\](other).generate[\TotalComparison\](
            LexicographicReduction,
            fn(a:E,b:E): TotalComparison => a CMP b) LEXICO
        (|self| CMP |other|)
    (** We give a specialized version of = because it can fail faster
        than CMP by checking sizes early. **)
    opr =(self,other:T): Boolean =
        (|self| = |other|) AND:
          (BIG AND [(a,b)<-self.zip[\E\](other)] a=b)
end

toArray[\E\](g:Indexed[\E,ZZ32\]): Array[\E,ZZ32\] = do
    bnds = g.bounds
    r = array[\E\](|bnds|).shift(bnds.lower)
    for (i,v) <- g.indexValuePairs do
        r.init(i,v)
    end
    r
  end

(** DelegatedIndexed is an Indexed generator that has recourse to
    another Indexed self.generator internally.  By default this in turn
    is defined in terms of self.indexValuePairs.  Thus it's only
    necessary to define either self.indexValuePairs or self.indices.

    This class is designed for convenience; it shouldn't be used as a
    type in runing code, but only as a supertype in lieu of Indexed.
**)
trait DelegatedIndexed[\E,I\] extends Indexed[\E,I\]
    getter generator(): Indexed[\E,I\] =
        self.indexValuePairs.map[\E\](fn (i:I, e:E): E => e)
    opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.indices|
    generate[\R\](r: Reduction[\R\], body: E->R): R =
        self.generator.generate[\R\](r,body)
    seq(self): SequentialGenerator[\E\] = seq(self.generator)
    cross[\G\](g: Generator[\G\]): Generator[\(E,G)\] =
        self.generator.cross[\G\](g)
    mapReduce[\R\](body: E->R, join:(R,R)->R, id:R): R =
        self.generator.mapReduce[\R\](body,join,id)
    reduce(j:(E,E)->E, z:E):E = self.generator.reduce(j,z)
    reduce(r: Reduction[\E\]):E = self.generator.reduce(r)
    loop(f:E->()): () = self.generator.loop(f)
end

(** The MutableIndexed trait is an indexed trait whose elements can be
    mutated using indexed assignment.  Right now we're using this type
    in a somewhat dangerous way, since eg Array1[\E,b0,s0\] extends
    both Indexed[\Array1[\E,b0,s0\],E,ZZ32\] and
    Indexed[\Array[\E,ZZ32\],E,ZZ32\].  We will need to find a
    solution to this at some point.
**)
trait MutableIndexed[\E, I\]
        extends { Indexed[\E,I\] }

(* Step-0 probe A (Pavol's caveat): can the duplicated ProbDist x Mat
   juxtaposition body be eliminated by a shared trait?

   Design A: a bare trait RowLike that carries the rank/indexed supertypes
   and NO members of its own (ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed already declare
   indices, |self| and [i] abstractly).  Vec and ProbDist extend RowLike;
   the juxtaposition body is written ONCE, at top level, on RowLike.

   Must coexist with the Mat x Vec direction, whose legality rests on
   Rank1 excludes Rank2 (FortressLibrary.fss:1599).  RowLike extends Rank1,
   so the exclusion should be inherited.

   Element type RR64 (no autodiff tape) -- overload resolution among
   carriers does not depend on the element type; shapes are microgpt2's. *)
component n1_rowlike_toplevel
import List.{...}
export Executable

trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
end

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\RR64\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] -u | u <- xs |>)
end

object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "ProbDist" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
end

opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): RR64 = SUM[m <- u.indices] (u[m] w[m])
opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] r DOT x | r <- w |>)

(* THE DEDUPLICATED OVERLOAD: one body, both Vec and ProbDist *)
opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec =
  Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
  Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u / c | u <- x |>)
opr -(x: Vec, s: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u - s | u <- x |>)
exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] exp u | u <- x |>)

softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
  e = exp(a - m)
  s = SUM[u <- e] u
  ProbDist(<|[\RR64\] u / s | u <- e |>)
end

(* microgpt2.fss:225 verbatim in shape *)
attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V

run() = do
  q  = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>)
  K  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.0, 1.0|>) |>)
  V  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 3.0, 4.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 5.0, 6.0|>) |>)
  println("softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = " softmax(q K^T / SQRT 2))
  println("attend = " attend(q, K, V, 2))
  (* both directions still work *)
  println("Mat x Vec = " (K V[0]))
  println("Vec x Mat = " (q K))
end

end

(* Step-0 probe A2: push the shared members INTO the trait.

   RowLike declares an abstract accessor (the underlying List) and defines
   indices, |self| and [i] in terms of it, exactly as MultiplicativeRing
   hands Value its inherited operators (complex_ring precedent).  Then
   ProbDist's whole body is empty: it is one line of source.

   Open question this probe settles: does an OBJECT VALUE PARAMETER
   (`object Vec(xs: List[..])`) satisfy a trait's ABSTRACT GETTER of the
   same name?  Spec basic/objects.tex: object value parameters are fields
   and fields have getters.

   Also exercised here, per the brief: opr = (both carriers), |x|,
   subscripting, generator integration (u <- x, BIG AND, zip), and the
   Mat x Vec direction that rests on Rank1 excludes Rank2. *)
component n2_rowlike_getter
import List.{...}
export Executable

trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter xs(): List[\RR64\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = (self.xs)[i]
end

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\RR64\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] -u | u <- xs |>)
  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] (xs[m] = y[m]))
end

(* the named space: ONE line *)
object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
end

opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): RR64 = SUM[m <- u.indices] (u[m] w[m])
opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] r DOT x | r <- w |>)

(* THE DEDUPLICATED OVERLOAD: one body, both Vec and ProbDist *)
opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec =
  Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
  Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u / c | u <- x |>)
opr -(x: Vec, s: RR64): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] u - s | u <- x |>)
exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<|[\RR64\] exp u | u <- x |>)

softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
  e = exp(a - m)
  ProbDist((e / (SUM[u <- e] u)).xs)
end

attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V

run() = do
  q  = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>)
  K  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.0, 1.0|>) |>)
  V  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 3.0, 4.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 5.0, 6.0|>) |>)
  p  = softmax(q K^T / SQRT 2)
  println("softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = " p)
  println("attend = " attend(q, K, V, 2))
  println("Mat x Vec = " (K V[0]))
  println("Vec x Mat = " (q K))
  (* the members the carriers rely on, on BOTH carriers *)
  println("|p| = " |p| "   p[0] = " p[0])
  println("SUM over p (generator) = " (SUM[u <- p] u))
  println("Vec = Vec (reflexive) : " (q = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>)))
  println("Mat = Mat (reflexive) : " (K = K))
  println("zip on Vec : " (q + q))
  println("p indices  : " (<|[\ZZ32\] j | j <- p.indices |>))
end

end

(* ---------- the carriers: library citizens ----------
   Vec/Mat wrap List; extending the library's own Rank1/Rank2 makes them
   mutually excluding, so BOTH juxtaposition directions are legal
   overloads; ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed buy |x|, x[i], zip, and full
   generator integration (u <- x, BIG ops over x) from three one-line
   members; AdditiveGroup gives Vec inherited binary minus and zero from
   + and unary -.  Carrier = is defined because HasRank's default
   equality is constant false -- even x = x. *)

object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\],
              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = xs[i]
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\Value\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] ((xs[m]).data = y[m].data))
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])

  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
