(* ---------- the carriers: library citizens ----------
   The carriers wrap List; extending the library's own Rank1/Rank2 makes
   rows and matrices mutually excluding, so BOTH juxtaposition directions
   are legal overloads; ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed buy |x|, x[i], zip,
   and full generator integration (u <- x, BIG ops over x) from three
   one-line members; AdditiveGroup gives Vec inherited binary minus and
   zero from + and unary -.  Carrier = is defined because HasRank's
   default equality is constant false -- even x = x.

   RowLike is the shared supertype of every rank-1 carrier.  It declares
   the underlying list as an abstract getter and defines indices, |.| and
   [.] once in terms of it -- the same move by which MultiplicativeRing
   hands Value its inherited operators.  Its purpose is dedup: the
   left-multiplication  p M  is written ONE time, on RowLike, and both
   Vec and ProbDist get it.  (An object's value parameter satisfies a
   trait's abstract getter of the same name; probed, n2/n4.)

   ProbDist is the simplex: softmax's codomain, the paper's own
   p in Delta^(n-1).  Because Fortress 1.0 has no working type alias
   (spec basic/types-vals-vars.tex:597-623 specifies
   `type ProbDist = Vec`, expanded before type checking and defining no
   new type; IndexBuilder.scala:187 stops one line short of it), naming
   the space costs a NEW NOMINAL TYPE.  With RowLike that cost is one
   declaration line and one lift at softmax's exit -- not a duplicated
   operator body. *)

trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\] }
  getter xs(): List[\Value\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = (self.xs)[i]
end

object Vec(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\Value\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] ((xs[m]).data = y[m].data))
end

object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
end

(* the KV cache: one Mat of history per head, indexed by head and
   extended at the right -- the paper's own noun, with the paper's own
   two operations.  It replaces the spelling List[\Mat\], which this file
   otherwise uses for the per-head WEIGHT bundles _Wq/_Wk/_Wv: the same
   type name meant two unrelated things, and needed a comment to say
   which. *)
object KVCache(heads: List[\Mat\])
    extends { ZeroIndexed[\Mat\], DelegatedIndexed[\Mat,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |heads|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|
  opr [h: ZZ32]: Mat = heads[h]
  extend(ks: List[\Vec\]): KVCache =
    KVCache(<| (heads[h]).addRight(ks[h]) | h <- self.indices |>)
end

emptyCache(nh: ZZ32): KVCache = KVCache(<| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>)

`(* the carriers: library citizens (Rank1 excludes Rank2 makes both
   juxtaposition directions legal under the Meet Rule) *)
object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\],
              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = xs[i]
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\Value\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] ((xs[m]).data = y[m].data))
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
end

(* the notation layer: each operator defined once, by its index formula *)
opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): Value = sum(<| u[m] w[m] | m <- u.indices |>)

opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| r DOT x | r <- w |>)

opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
  Vec(<| sum(<| p[j] (m[j])[c] | j <- p.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
  Mat(<| Vec(<| (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr -(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u - s | u <- x |>)
opr /(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u / s | u <- x |>)
opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| u / c | u <- x |>)
relu(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| relu u | u <- x |>)
exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| exp u | u <- x |>)
concat(heads: List[\Vec\]): Vec = Vec(<| u | h <- heads, u <- h |>)`
===sheet-engine===
`object Value(var data: RR64, children: List[\Value\], grads: List[\RR64\])
       extends { MultiplicativeRing[\Value\], StandardMax[\Value\] }
  getter one(): Value = konst(1.0)
  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
  var visited: Boolean := false
  opr +(self, o: Value): Value = Value(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
  opr TIMES(self, o: Value): Value =
    Value(data o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
  opr -(self): Value = Value(-data, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
  opr /(self, o: Value): Value =
    Value(data / o.data, <| self, o |>,
          <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
  opr ^ (self, n: RR64): Value = Value(data^n, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
  opr MAX(self, o: Value): Value = if data >= o.data then self else o end
end

sum(addends: List[\Value\]): Value =
  Value(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)
sum(x: Vec): Value = sum(x.xs)

backward(root: Value): () = do
  t = Topo()
  t.build(root)
  root.grad := 1.0
  for v <- seq(t.items.reverse) do
    for (ch, lg) <- seq(v.children.zip[\RR64\](v.grads)) do
      ch.grad := ch.grad + lg v.grad
    end
  end
  for v <- t.items do v.visited := false end
end`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Segment line counts for Karpathy's microgpt.py and the Fortress cores.

Python is counted on the raw file with comments/blank lines filtered.
The Fortress files are counted on their already-stripped cores (strip.py),
so both sides carry exactly comments-out, blanks-out, verification-out.
"""
import sys

SEGS = ["boilerplate/imports", "data + tokenizer", "autodiff engine",
        "notation layer", "model blocks", "config + weight init",
        "optimizer (Adam) + training loop", "sampling + inference"]


def code_lines(path, pyth):
    out = {}
    for i, l in enumerate(open(path).read().split("\n"), 1):
        s = l.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        if pyth and s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        out[i] = l
    return out


def tally(lines, ranges):
    t = [0] * len(SEGS)

content.content:
\note{I think this should be phrased differently.
When I originally read that, I took it to mean
that fields were always ``private.'' -- Scott}
Fields are variables local to an object.
They must not be referred to outside their enclosing object declarations.
Each field is either a non-transient value parameter of a constructor
declaration, or it is explicitly defined by a field declaration within the body of a constructor
declaration, a singleton declaration, or an object expression
(described in \secref{object-expr}).
A field declaration in an object declaration is syntactically identical to
a top-level variable declaration (described in \secref{top-var-decls}),
with the same meanings attached to the form of variable declarations.
Additional modifiers apply to fields, as described in \secref{abstract-fields}.  Unlike with an abstract field in a trait declaration, an object declaration may declare a \KWD{hidden} field which is not \KWD{settable}.

Each field declaration includes an \emph{initial-value} expression,
which specifies the initial value of that field.
Field initialization occurs in textual program order:
evaluation of each initial-value expression
must complete before evaluation of the next initial-value expression,
and all previous field names
(and the parameters of the constructor,
in a constructor declaration)
are in scope when evaluating an initial-value expression
(see~\secref{scope}).
All fields of an object are initialized
before that object is made available for subsequent computation;
thus,
it is illegal to invoke methods on
an object being initialized:
\KWD{self} is \emph{not} implicitly declared by a field declaration.

\end{Grammar}


Traits may also include abstract field declarations that are implicit
declarations of abstract getter methods.
Syntactically, an abstract field declaration consists of an optional
sequence of modifiers followed by the field name, followed by the token
`\EXP{\COLONOP}', and the type of the field.


By default, a field declaration implicitly
declares a getter method for the field unless there is an explicit
getter declared in the enclosing trait.
An implicit getter method takes no arguments, has the same name as the
field, and has a return type equal to the field type.  When called, the
implicit getter returns the value of the field when called.




Abstract field declarations can include the following special modifiers:
\paragraph{\KWD{hidden}:}
A field declaration with the
modifier \KWD{hidden} has no implicit getter method.


\paragraph{\KWD{settable}:}
A field declaration with the modifier \KWD{settable} has an implicit
setter method unless there is an explicit setter declared in the enclosing
trait.  An implicit setter method takes a parameter
(with no default expression) whose type is the type of the field, and
returns \EXP{()}. When called, the implicit setter rebinds the
corresponding field to its argument.
If a field declaration includes the modifier  \KWD{settable} and
\KWD{hidden}, only an abstract setter is declared.

delivered one (215), the no-dedup counterfactual (221), and a KVCache-only
variant (213). The whole cost lands in the math half — the harness is
byte-for-byte untouched, which is the right place for a change that is

**Pavol's caveat is answered: yes, traits eliminate the duplication.** Four
independent designs work; the adopted one costs `ProbDist` **two lines** —

report's predicted six-plus-a-duplicated-operator-body.

## Step 0 — the mandated probe: can a trait kill the duplicated `ProbDist × Mat` body?

### The question

`aliases-units-report.md` Q3.2 case 2 costed `ProbDist` at "one 6-line carrier
**plus one duplicated juxtaposition body** — the `ProbDist × Mat` overload is a
verbatim copy of the `Vec × Mat` one, because the two carriers share no
supertype carrying that operation." Pavol: *"can't this be eliminated by using
other features of Fortress type system like traits?"*

The precedent named in the plan file's Verified facts is
`MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` handing `Value` its inherited operators
(`explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The structural risk to check is whether an
intermediate trait breaks the mechanism the flagship line rests on —
`Rank1 excludes Rank2` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1599`), which is what makes both
`Mat × Vec` and `Vec × Mat` legal overloads under the spec's Meet Rule.

### Spec consulted first

- `Specification/basic/traits.tex:573-583` — *"Traits may also include
  **abstract field declarations** that are implicit declarations of abstract
  getter methods… By default, a field declaration implicitly declares a getter
  method for the field unless there is an explicit getter declared in the
  enclosing trait."*
- `Specification/basic/objects.tex:271` — *"Each field is either a
  **non-transient value parameter of a constructor declaration**, or it is
  explicitly defined by a field declaration…"*

Together these sanction exactly the move needed: a trait declares `xs` as an
abstract field, and `object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])` satisfies it with its own
value parameter, at zero extra lines.

- `FortressLibrary.fss:1599` — `trait Rank1 extends { Rank[\1\] } excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }`. A trait extending `Rank1` inherits the exclusion, so the Meet Rule should still separate the two juxtaposition overloads.
- `FortressLibrary.fss:1766-1780` — `DelegatedIndexed` supplies `opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.indices|` as a default (relevant below).

### Four designs, all four run

Probes are in this directory; all outputs in `probe-run.log`. Each is derived
from `explorations/alias-units-probes/p14_named_spaces.fss` as instructed
(element type `RR64`, no autodiff tape — overload resolution among carriers
does not depend on the element type, and the shapes are microgpt2's).

Every probe runs the flagship line **verbatim in shape**:

```
attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
```

and prints values that match the report's hand-verified numbers exactly
(`softmax = [0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431]`;
`attend = [3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686]`).

#### Design A — `n1_rowlike_toplevel.fss`: bare trait, operator at top level

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
end

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] } … end
object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } … end

opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = …
opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec = …      (* written ONCE *)
```

The trait carries only the supertypes; `ZeroIndexed`/`DelegatedIndexed` already
declare `indices`, `|self|`, `[i]` abstractly, so each object still supplies
them. Verbatim output:

```
softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = ProbDist<|0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431|>
attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
```

**Works, first try.** Both juxtaposition directions coexist: the exclusion is
inherited through `RowLike`, so the Meet of `(Mat, Vec)` and `(RowLike, Mat)`
is empty in the second position.

#### Design A2 — `n2_rowlike_getter.fss`: push the shared members into the trait

The one that shrinks the file. The trait declares the underlying list as an
**explicit abstract getter** and defines the three indexed members once:

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter xs(): List[\RR64\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = (self.xs)[i]
end
…
object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } end      (* ONE line *)
```

This probe also exercises, per the brief, everything the carriers rely on —
`opr =` on both carriers, `|x|`, subscripting, `zip`, generator integration —
on both sides of the trait. Verbatim output:

```
softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = 0.6697615493266569,0.3302384506733431
attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
|p| = 2   p[0] = 0.6697615493266569
SUM over p (generator) = 1.0
Vec = Vec (reflexive) : true
Mat = Mat (reflexive) : true
zip on Vec : Vec<|2.0, 0.0|>
p indices  : <|0, 1|>
```

**Nothing breaks.** In particular `opr =` still works on both carriers — the
`HasRank` reflexive-false landmine (judgment decision 9) is still correctly
overridden through the intermediate trait, `x = x` is `true`, and generator
integration (`SUM[u <- p]`, `p.indices`) works on the object whose members are
*inherited* rather than declared.

*(Note the `ProbDist` printout has no `Vec…`/`ProbDist…` wrapper here: with no
`asString` getter, `DelegatedIndexed`'s default prints bare. microgpt2 has no
`asString` getters — the diet removed them as dead — and nothing prints a
carrier, so this is cosmetic to the probe only.)*

#### Design B — `n3_rowlike_method.fss`: the operator as a functional method on the trait

The brief's named alternative. `self` in first parameter position:

```
trait RowLike extends { … }
  …
  opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat): Vec =
    Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- self.indices] (self[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
end
```

```
attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
```

**Also works** — a functional-method `juxtaposition` legally coexists with the
top-level `Mat × Vec` one. Rejected for microgpt2 on notation grounds only:
it would put one direction of juxtaposition inside a trait body while its twin
sits in the notation layer, and the render sheet's whole claim is *"each
operator defined once, by its index formula"*, in one place.

#### Design C — `n4_rowlike_comprises.fss`: A2 plus a `comprises` clause

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
    comprises { Vec, ProbDist }
```

Identical output to A2 (see `probe-run.log`). **Works.** Not adopted: it costs
a line, lists the carrier roster a second time, and buys exhaustiveness nothing
here needs.

#### Design A3 (adopted) — `n6_rowlike_absfield.fss`: the spec's own abstract-field form

`getter xs(): List[\RR64\]` replaced by the spec's terser idiom
(`basic/traits.tex:573-583`):

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  xs: List[\RR64\]
  …
```

Identical output to A2. **Works, and it is the spec's own construct** — the
order-of-authority rule prefers it, it is shorter, and it renders as
`xs: List⟦Value⟧`, which visually mirrors `object Vec(xs: List⟦Value⟧)`. This
is what shipped.

### Step 0 verdict

**Dedup works; it is not close.** Four mechanisms, four green runs, no dead
ends to classify — the "no single-data-point rules" bar is met several times
over. Nothing in the carriers' contract breaks: `opr =`, `|x|`, `x[i]`, `zip`,
generator integration and `AdditiveGroup` inheritance all survive an
intermediate trait, and `Rank1 excludes Rank2` still separates the two
juxtaposition overloads when one of them is stated on a `Rank1` *subtrait*.

**Measured saving: 6 lines and one verbatim duplicated operator body.**
`microgpt2_nodedup.fss` (built here, golden-green) is 221 stripped lines
against the delivered 215.

**What this does to the page's exhibit.** The report proposed the duplicated
overload *as* the price tag of the missing `type` alias. That exhibit is not
lost — it is sharpened, and it becomes honest rather than overstated:

> Fortress specifies transparent type aliases — `type ProbDist = Vec`,
> expanded before type checking, defining no new type
> (`basic/types-vals-vars.tex:597-623`) — and the 2012 implementation stops one
> line short of them (`IndexBuilder.scala:187`, with the expansion at
> `TypeAnalyzer.scala:552-557` already written and unreachable). So a Fortress
> signature can name a space only by minting a **new nominal type**. Minting
> costs something, and the language is good enough to make it cheap: a shared
> supertype writes the operator once, and `ProbDist` costs **two lines** —
> `trait RowLike` and `object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end`.
> The alias would have cost **zero**, and would have needed no lift at
> softmax's exit. Both files exist and both pass the golden check; the
> difference is six lines.

---

## Step 1 — `KVCache`

### The change

```
object KVCache(heads: List[\Mat\])
    extends { ZeroIndexed[\Mat\], DelegatedIndexed[\Mat,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |heads|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|
  opr [h: ZZ32]: Mat = heads[h]
  extend(ks: List[\Vec\]): KVCache =
    KVCache(<| (heads[h]).addRight(ks[h]) | h <- self.indices |>)
end

emptyCache(nh: ZZ32): KVCache = KVCache(<| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>)
```

and, in `Model`:

```
- forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
-     : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
+ forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: KVCache, vh: KVCache): (Vec, KVCache, KVCache) = do
    …
-   K = <| (kh[h]).addRight(_Wk[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
-   V = <| (vh[h]).addRight(_Wv[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
+   K = kh.extend(<| _Wk[h] x2 | h <- 0#nHead |>)
+   V = vh.extend(<| _Wv[h] x2 | h <- 0#nHead |>)
```

`emptyHist` is gone; the three `var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(n), emptyHist(n))`
declarations (goldenCheck, training loop, inference loop) become
`var (kh, vh): (KVCache, KVCache) := (emptyCache(n), emptyCache(n))`.

### Line accounting — measured, not estimated

Built `microgpt2_kvonly.fss`: the shipped 206-line file with **only** Step 1
applied. Stripped: **213**. So `KVCache` is **+7**, decomposed:

| | lines |
|---|---|
| the carrier object | +8 |
| `emptyCache` | +1 |
| `emptyHist` removed | −1 |
| `forward` signature: two lines → one | −1 |
| the two extension comprehensions | **±0** — still two lines, now `kh.extend(…)` instead of reaching inside with `(kh[h]).addRight(…)` |
| the three `var (kh, vh)` declarations | ±0 (shorter, same count) |
| **net** | **+7** |

**The report's "net negative lines" is wrong**, and it is worth recording *why*,
because it is a repeatable estimation error: the prediction listed everything
the carrier *removes* (`emptyHist`, the extension comprehensions, the wide
signature) and did not price the carrier itself. The extension comprehensions
in particular do not vanish — there are two cache directions and they stay two
lines; what changes is that the line stops reaching into the cache's
representation.

**What the +7 buys, stated plainly** (the honest case, since it is not free):

- The file's one genuine type ambiguity is gone. `List[\Mat\]` spelled both the
  per-head **weight** bundles (`_Wq, _Wk, _Wv`) and the per-head **KV history**;
  a reader had to consult a comment to tell which a signature meant.
- `forward`'s type is now readable at a glance and fits on one line:
  `(Vec, KVCache, KVCache)`.
- Extension is one named operation with the paper's own name, on the paper's
  own noun, instead of an inlined `addRight` into an indexed member.

**One line is available and deliberately not taken.** `KVCache`'s
`opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|` is provably dead (nothing in the file takes the
length of a cache) and `DelegatedIndexed` supplies `|self| = |self.indices|` as
a default — verified by probe `n5_kvcache_nolen.fss`, which drops the member
and still runs:

```
K after two steps = KVCache<|Mat<|Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>, Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>|>, Mat<|Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>, Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>|>|>
|K2[0]| = 2
```

Rejected for carrier uniformity: the file's own header sentence is that
`ZeroIndexed`/`DelegatedIndexed` buy the carrier's whole interface "from three
one-line members", and `Vec`/`Mat` both declare all three. Breaking the pattern
in one carrier to save one line would cost more in the render sheet than it
saves in the count. Recorded so the option is on the table if the page wants it.

## Step 2 — `ProbDist`

### The change

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\] }
  xs: List[\Value\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = (self.xs)[i]
end

object Vec(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = …
  opr -(self): Vec = …
  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean = …
end

object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end
```

```
- opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
+ opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec =
    Vec(<| sum(<| p[j] (m[j])[c] | j <- p.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

- softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do
+ softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
    m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
    e = exp(a - m)
-   e / sum(e)
+   ProbDist((e / sum(e)).xs)
  end

- sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do
+ sample(p: ProbDist): ZZ32 = do
```

`nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value` is **unchanged** — as specified. Its body
`p = softmax(logits)` now binds a `ProbDist` and `p[y]` reaches it through
`RowLike`; not one character of the loss block moved, while `p` quietly became
a distribution. That is a nice small exhibit in itself.

## Traps and findings worth carrying

1. **An object's value parameter satisfies a trait's abstract field.** Both the
   explicit form (`getter xs(): List[\Value\]`) and the spec's terser abstract
   field (`xs: List[\Value\]`) work, and `object Vec(xs: …)` needs no extra
   member to supply either. Spec: `basic/traits.tex:573-583` +
   `basic/objects.tex:271`. This is the mechanism that makes carrier dedup free.
2. **A `Rank1` subtrait inherits the `excludes`.** Stating an overload on
   `RowLike` (not on `Vec`) keeps both juxtaposition directions legal — the Meet
   Rule sees `RowLike ∩ Mat = ∅` through `Rank1 excludes Rank2`. Two independent
   confirmations (A/A2 and B), plus a third via `comprises` (C).
3. **`comprises` on such a trait is legal and inert here** — worth knowing it
   parses and runs, since the spec's exhaustiveness machinery is otherwise
   little exercised in this tree.
4. **A functional-method operator (`opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat)`) coexists
   with a top-level overload of the same operator.** Design B. Useful the next
   time an operator wants a home inside a trait.
5. **`DelegatedIndexed` supplies `opr |self|` for free** (`= |self.indices|`,
   `FortressLibrary.fss:1768`). Every carrier in this file declares it anyway;
   at least one declaration is provably dead. Probed: `n5_kvcache_nolen.fss`.
6. **Estimation trap, recorded against the previous round:** costing a carrier
   by what it deletes and not by what it is. `KVCache` was forecast net-negative
   and is +7. When a future report prices a carrier, price the object body first.
7. **`bin/fortick` leaves a `.tex` in the figure directory.** Delete it after
   rendering or it shows up as an untracked file.

variant (213). The whole cost lands in the math half — the harness is

**Pavol's caveat is answered: yes, traits eliminate the duplication.** Four

---

## Step 0 — the mandated probe: can a trait kill the duplicated `ProbDist x Mat` body?

### The question

`aliases-units-report.md` Q3.2 case 2 costed `ProbDist` at "one 6-line carrier
**plus one duplicated juxtaposition body** — the `ProbDist x Mat` overload is a
verbatim copy of the `Vec x Mat` one, because the two carriers share no
supertype carrying that operation." Pavol: *"can't this be eliminated by using
other features of Fortress type system like traits?"*

The precedent named in the plan file's Verified facts is
`MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` handing `Value` its inherited operators
(`explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The structural risk to check is whether an
intermediate trait breaks the mechanism the flagship line rests on —
`Rank1 excludes Rank2` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1599`), which is what makes both
`Mat x Vec` and `Vec x Mat` legal overloads under the spec's Meet Rule.

### Spec consulted first

- `Specification/basic/traits.tex:573-583` — *"Traits may also include
  **abstract field declarations** that are implicit declarations of abstract
  getter methods... By default, a field declaration implicitly declares a getter
  method for the field unless there is an explicit getter declared in the
  enclosing trait."*
- `Specification/basic/objects.tex:271` — *"Each field is either a
  **non-transient value parameter of a constructor declaration**, or it is
  explicitly defined by a field declaration..."*

Together these sanction exactly the move needed: a trait declares `xs` as an
abstract field, and `object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])` satisfies it with its own
value parameter, at zero extra lines.

- `FortressLibrary.fss:1599` — `trait Rank1 extends { Rank[\1\] } excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }`.
  A trait extending `Rank1` inherits the exclusion, so the Meet Rule should
  still separate the two juxtaposition overloads.
- `FortressLibrary.fss:1766-1780` — `DelegatedIndexed` supplies
  `opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.indices|` as a default (relevant below).

### Four designs, all four run

Probes are in this directory; all outputs in `probe-run.log`. Each is derived
from `explorations/alias-units-probes/p14_named_spaces.fss` as instructed
(element type `RR64`, no autodiff tape — overload resolution among carriers
does not depend on the element type, and the shapes are microgpt2's).

Every probe runs the flagship line **verbatim in shape**:

    attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V

and prints values matching the report's hand-verified numbers exactly
(`softmax = [0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431]`;
`attend = [3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686]`).

#### Design A — `n1_rowlike_toplevel.fss`: bare trait, operator at top level

    trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
    end

    object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] } ... end
    object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } ... end

    opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = ...
    opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec = ...      (* written ONCE *)

The trait carries only the supertypes; `ZeroIndexed`/`DelegatedIndexed` already
declare `indices`, `|self|`, `[i]` abstractly, so each object still supplies
them. Verbatim output:

    softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = ProbDist<|0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431|>
    attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
    Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
    Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>

**Works, first try.** Both juxtaposition directions coexist: the exclusion is
inherited through `RowLike`, so the Meet of `(Mat, Vec)` and `(RowLike, Mat)`
is empty in the second position.

#### Design A2 — `n2_rowlike_getter.fss`: push the shared members into the trait

The one that shrinks the file. The trait declares the underlying list as an
**explicit abstract getter** and defines the three indexed members once:

    trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
      getter xs(): List[\RR64\]
      getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
      opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
      opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = (self.xs)[i]
    end
    ...
    object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } end      (* ONE line *)

This probe also exercises, per the brief, everything the carriers rely on —
`opr =` on both carriers, `|x|`, subscripting, `zip`, generator integration.
Verbatim output:

    softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = 0.6697615493266569,0.3302384506733431
    attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
    Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
    Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
    |p| = 2   p[0] = 0.6697615493266569
    SUM over p (generator) = 1.0
    Vec = Vec (reflexive) : true
    Mat = Mat (reflexive) : true
    zip on Vec : Vec<|2.0, 0.0|>
    p indices  : <|0, 1|>

**Nothing breaks.** In particular `opr =` still works on both carriers — the
`HasRank` reflexive-false landmine (judgment decision 9) is still correctly
overridden through the intermediate trait, `x = x` is `true`, and generator
integration (`SUM[u <- p]`, `p.indices`) works on the object whose members are
*inherited* rather than declared.

*(The `ProbDist` printout has no wrapper here: with no `asString` getter,
`DelegatedIndexed`'s default prints bare. microgpt2 has no `asString` getters —
the diet removed them as dead — and nothing prints a carrier, so this is
cosmetic to the probe only.)*

#### Design B — `n3_rowlike_method.fss`: the operator as a functional method on the trait

The brief's named alternative. `self` in first parameter position:

    trait RowLike extends { ... }
      ...
      opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat): Vec =
        Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- self.indices] (self[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
    end

    attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
    Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
    Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>

**Also works** — a functional-method `juxtaposition` legally coexists with the
top-level `Mat x Vec` one. Rejected for microgpt2 on notation grounds only: it
would put one direction of juxtaposition inside a trait body while its twin
sits in the notation layer, and the render sheet's whole claim is *"each
operator defined once, by its index formula"*, in one place.

#### Design C — `n4_rowlike_comprises.fss`: A2 plus a `comprises` clause

    trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
        comprises { Vec, ProbDist }

Identical output to A2 (see `probe-run.log`). **Works.** Not adopted: it costs
a line, lists the carrier roster a second time, and buys exhaustiveness nothing
here needs.

#### Design A3 (adopted) — `n6_rowlike_absfield.fss`: the spec's own abstract-field form

`getter xs(): List[\RR64\]` replaced by the spec's terser idiom
(`basic/traits.tex:573-583`):

    trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
      xs: List[\RR64\]
      ...

Identical output to A2. **Works, and it is the spec's own construct** — the
order-of-authority rule prefers it, it is shorter, and it renders as
`xs: List[[Value]]`, which visually mirrors `object Vec(xs: List[[Value]])`.
This is what shipped.

### Step 0 verdict

**Dedup works; it is not close.** Four mechanisms, four green runs, no dead
ends to classify — the "no single-data-point rules" bar is met several times
over. Nothing in the carriers' contract breaks: `opr =`, `|x|`, `x[i]`, `zip`,
generator integration and `AdditiveGroup` inheritance all survive an
intermediate trait, and `Rank1 excludes Rank2` still separates the two
juxtaposition overloads when one of them is stated on a `Rank1` *subtrait*.

**Measured saving: 6 lines and one verbatim duplicated operator body.**
`microgpt2_nodedup.fss` (built here, golden-green) is 221 stripped lines
against the delivered 215.

**What this does to the page's exhibit.** The report proposed the duplicated
overload *as* the price tag of the missing `type` alias. That exhibit is not
lost — it is sharpened, and it becomes honest rather than overstated:

> Fortress specifies transparent type aliases — `type ProbDist = Vec`, expanded
> before type checking, defining no new type
> (`basic/types-vals-vars.tex:597-623`) — and the 2012 implementation stops one
> line short of them (`IndexBuilder.scala:187`, with the expansion at
> `TypeAnalyzer.scala:552-557` already written and unreachable). So a Fortress
> signature can name a space only by minting a **new nominal type**. Minting
> costs something, and the language is good enough to make it cheap: a shared
> supertype writes the operator once, and `ProbDist` costs **two lines** —
> `trait RowLike` and
> `object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end`. The alias would
> have cost **zero**, and would have needed no lift at softmax's exit. Both
> files exist and both pass the golden check; the difference is six lines.

---

## Step 1 — `KVCache`

### The change

    object KVCache(heads: List[\Mat\])
        extends { ZeroIndexed[\Mat\], DelegatedIndexed[\Mat,ZZ32\] }
      getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |heads|
      opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|
      opr [h: ZZ32]: Mat = heads[h]
      extend(ks: List[\Vec\]): KVCache =
        KVCache(<| (heads[h]).addRight(ks[h]) | h <- self.indices |>)
    end

    emptyCache(nh: ZZ32): KVCache = KVCache(<| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>)

and, in `Model`:

    - forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
    -     : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
    + forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: KVCache, vh: KVCache): (Vec, KVCache, KVCache) = do
        ...
    -   K = <| (kh[h]).addRight(_Wk[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
    -   V = <| (vh[h]).addRight(_Wv[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
    +   K = kh.extend(<| _Wk[h] x2 | h <- 0#nHead |>)
    +   V = vh.extend(<| _Wv[h] x2 | h <- 0#nHead |>)

`emptyHist` is gone; the three
`var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(n), emptyHist(n))`
declarations (goldenCheck, training loop, inference loop) become
`var (kh, vh): (KVCache, KVCache) := (emptyCache(n), emptyCache(n))`.

### Line accounting — measured, not estimated

Built `microgpt2_kvonly.fss`: the shipped 206-line file with **only** Step 1
applied. Stripped: **213**. So `KVCache` is **+7**, decomposed:

| | lines |
|---|---|
| the carrier object | +8 |
| `emptyCache` | +1 |
| `emptyHist` removed | -1 |
| `forward` signature: two lines -> one | -1 |
| the two extension comprehensions | **+-0** — still two lines, now `kh.extend(...)` instead of reaching inside with `(kh[h]).addRight(...)` |
| the three `var (kh, vh)` declarations | +-0 (shorter, same count) |
| **net** | **+7** |

**The report's "net negative lines" is wrong**, and it is worth recording *why*,
because it is a repeatable estimation error: the prediction listed everything
the carrier *removes* (`emptyHist`, the extension comprehensions, the wide
signature) and did not price the carrier itself. The extension comprehensions in
particular do not vanish — there are two cache directions and they stay two
lines; what changes is that the line stops reaching into the cache's
representation.

**What the +7 buys, stated plainly** (the honest case, since it is not free):

- The file's one genuine type ambiguity is gone. `List[\Mat\]` spelled both the
  per-head **weight** bundles (`_Wq, _Wk, _Wv`) and the per-head **KV history**;
  a reader had to consult a comment to tell which a signature meant.
- `forward`'s type is now readable at a glance and fits on one line:
  `(Vec, KVCache, KVCache)`.
- Extension is one named operation with the paper's own name, on the paper's own
  noun, instead of an inlined `addRight` into an indexed member.

**One line is available and deliberately not taken.** `KVCache`'s
`opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|` is provably dead (nothing in the file takes the
length of a cache) and `DelegatedIndexed` supplies `|self| = |self.indices|` as
a default — verified by probe `n5_kvcache_nolen.fss`, which drops the member and
still runs:

    K after two steps = KVCache<|Mat<|Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>, Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>|>, Mat<|Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>, Vec<|1.0, 2.0|>|>|>
    |K2[0]| = 2

## Step 2 — `ProbDist`

### The change

    trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\] }
      xs: List[\Value\]
      getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
      opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
      opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = (self.xs)[i]
    end

    object Vec(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
      opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = ...
      opr -(self): Vec = ...
      opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean = ...
    end

    object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end

    - opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
    + opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec =
        Vec(<| sum(<| p[j] (m[j])[c] | j <- p.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

    - softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do
    + softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
        m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
        e = exp(a - m)
    -   e / sum(e)
    +   ProbDist((e / sum(e)).xs)
      end

    - sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do
    + sample(p: ProbDist): ZZ32 = do

`nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value` is **unchanged** — as specified. Its body
`p = softmax(logits)` now binds a `ProbDist` and `p[y]` reaches it through
`RowLike`; not one character of the loss block moved, while `p` quietly became a
distribution. That is a small exhibit in itself.

### The flagship line is verbatim

    attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V

Character-identical to the shipped file (`explorations/microgpt2.fss:267`), and
`explorations/fortify/block-attention.{tic,-light.svg,-dark.svg}` were **not
regenerated** — `git status` shows them unmodified. Its meaning is strictly
richer: `softmax(...) V` now resolves to `RowLike x Mat` with a `ProbDist` on
the left, and the resolution is the *same definition* the `q K^T` on the same
line uses.

| `trait RowLike` | +6 |
| `Vec` loses its three indexed members and its 3-line `extends` clause collapses to one | -5 |

= **221 stripped lines**, i.e. **+8** on top of the KVCache-only 213.

**Dedup saving: 6 lines, and the duplicated operator body never exists.**

### The one residue: the lift at softmax's exit

`ProbDist((e / sum(e)).xs)` unwraps a `Vec` and relabels it. It is the only
place in the file where a carrier's representation is touched outside the
carrier's own body, and it exists solely because `ProbDist` is a *new nominal
type* rather than an alias. Alternatives considered:

- `s = sum(e)` then `ProbDist(<| u / s | u <- e |>)` — costs a line and, worse,

- reusing `opr /(x: Vec, s: Value)` to return `ProbDist` — impossible: `rmsnorm`

`type ProbDist = Vec` the line would read `e / sum(e)` and the whole trait would

1. **An object's value parameter satisfies a trait's abstract field.** Both the
   explicit form (`getter xs(): List[\Value\]`) and the spec's terser abstract

   member to supply either. Spec: `basic/traits.tex:573-583` +
   `basic/objects.tex:271`. This is the mechanism that makes carrier dedup free.
2. **A `Rank1` subtrait inherits the `excludes`.** Stating an overload on
   `RowLike` (not on `Vec`) keeps both juxtaposition directions legal — the Meet
   Rule sees `RowLike ^ Mat = empty` through `Rank1 excludes Rank2`. Two
   independent confirmations (A/A2 and B), plus a third via `comprises` (C).
3. **`comprises` on such a trait is legal and inert here** — worth knowing it
   parses and runs, since the spec's exhaustiveness machinery is otherwise
   little exercised in this tree.
4. **A functional-method operator (`opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat)`) coexists
   with a top-level overload of the same operator.** Design B. Useful the next
   time an operator wants a home inside a trait.
5. **`DelegatedIndexed` supplies `opr |self|` for free** (`= |self.indices|`,
   `FortressLibrary.fss:1768`). Every carrier in this file declares it anyway; at
   least one declaration is provably dead. Probed: `n5_kvcache_nolen.fss`.
6. **Estimation trap, recorded against the previous round:** costing a carrier by
   what it deletes and not by what it is. `KVCache` was forecast net-negative and
   is +7. When a future report prices a carrier, price the object body first.
7. **`bin/fortick` leaves a `.tex` in the figure directory.** Delete it after

## Step 0 — the mandated probe

### Spec consulted first
- `Specification/basic/traits.tex:573-583` — *"Traits may also include **abstract field declarations** that are implicit declarations of abstract getter methods… a field declaration implicitly declares a getter method for the field unless there is an explicit getter declared in the enclosing trait."*
- `Specification/basic/objects.tex:271` — *"Each field is either a **non-transient value parameter of a constructor declaration**, or it is explicitly defined by a field declaration…"*

Together these sanction exactly the move needed: the trait declares `xs` abstractly; `object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])` satisfies it with its own value parameter, at zero extra lines.
- `FortressLibrary.fss:1599` — `trait Rank1 … excludes { Rank2, Rank3, Number, String }`; a subtrait inherits the exclusion.
- `FortressLibrary.fss:1766-1780` — `DelegatedIndexed` supplies `opr |self| = |self.indices|` as a default.

### Four designs, all four run
All derived from `p14_named_spaces.fss` (element type `RR64`; overload resolution among carriers does not depend on element type). All run the flagship line verbatim in shape and reproduce the report's hand-verified numbers exactly. Full outputs in `probe-run.log`.

**Design A — `n1_rowlike_toplevel.fss`** (bare trait, operator at top level):
```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] } end
object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] } … end
object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\]) extends { RowLike } … end
opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = …
opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec = …      (* written ONCE *)
```
```
softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = ProbDist<|0.6697615493266569, 0.3302384506733431|>
attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
```
Works, first try. Both juxtaposition directions coexist — the Meet of `(Mat, Vec)` and `(RowLike, Mat)` is empty in the second position because the exclusion is inherited.

**Design A2 — `n2_rowlike_getter.fss`** (shared members pushed into the trait; the one that shrinks the file):
```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter xs(): List[\RR64\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = (self.xs)[i]

…

```
Exercises everything the brief listed:
```
softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = 0.6697615493266569,0.3302384506733431
attend = Vec<|3.6604769013466862, 4.660476901346686|>
Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>

Mat = Mat (reflexive) : true

**Nothing breaks.** `opr =` still overrides the `HasRank` reflexive-false landmine through the intermediate trait (`x = x` is `true`); `|x|`, subscripting, `zip`, and generator integration all work on the object whose members are *inherited* rather than declared. (The bare `ProbDist` printout is `DelegatedIndexed`'s default `asString`; microgpt2 has no `asString` getters and prints no carrier, so this is cosmetic to the probe.)

**Design B — `n3_rowlike_method.fss`** (the operator as a functional method on the trait, `self` in first position):
```
  opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat): Vec =
    Vec(<|[\RR64\] SUM[j <- self.indices] (self[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
```

Mat x Vec = Vec<|3.0, 4.0|>
Vec x Mat = Vec<|1.0, 0.0|>
```

Rejected on notation grounds only: it would hide one juxtaposition direction inside a trait body while its twin sits in the notation layer, against the render sheet's claim that each operator is defined once, in one place.

**Design C — `n4_rowlike_comprises.fss`** (A2 + `comprises { Vec, ProbDist }`): identical output. Works. Not adopted — costs a line, lists the roster twice, buys exhaustiveness nothing needs.

**Dedup works; it is not close.** Four mechanisms, four green runs, no dead ends to classify. Measured saving: **6 lines and one verbatim duplicated operator body**.

## Step 2 — `ProbDist`

```
trait RowLike extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\] }
  xs: List[\Value\]
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |self.xs|
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |self.xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = (self.xs)[i]
end
object Vec(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike, AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] } … end
object ProbDist(xs: List[\Value\]) extends { RowLike } end

- opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
+ opr juxtaposition(p: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec =
- softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do  …  e / sum(e)
+ softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do  …  ProbDist((e / sum(e)).xs)
- sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do
+ sample(p: ProbDist): ZZ32 = do
```

`nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value` is **unchanged**, as specified — not one character of the loss block moved while `p` quietly became a distribution.

## Traps and findings worth carrying

1. **An object's value parameter satisfies a trait's abstract field.** Both `getter xs(): List[\Value\]` and the spec's terser `xs: List[\Value\]` work; `object Vec(xs: …)` needs no extra member. Spec: `basic/traits.tex:573-583` + `basic/objects.tex:271`. This is what makes carrier dedup free.
2. **A `Rank1` subtrait inherits the `excludes`.** Stating an overload on `RowLike` rather than `Vec` keeps both juxtaposition directions legal. Three independent confirmations (A/A2, B, C).
3. **`comprises` on such a trait is legal and inert here** — the spec's exhaustiveness machinery is otherwise little exercised in this tree.
4. **A functional-method operator (`opr juxtaposition(self, m: Mat)`) coexists with a top-level overload of the same operator.**
5. **`DelegatedIndexed` supplies `opr |self|` for free** (`= |self.indices|`). Every carrier here declares it anyway; at least one declaration is provably dead (`n5_kvcache_nolen.fss`).
6. **Estimation trap:** costing a carrier by what it deletes, not by what it is. `KVCache` was forecast net-negative and is +7. Price the object body first.
7. **`bin/fortick` leaves a `.tex` beside the `.tic`.** Three strays were created and deleted; `git status` is clean.
